433	
434	# Part III. Consequences and discriminating examples
435	
436	## Historical acyclicity does not imply semantic acyclicity
437	
438	**Claim.** An inquiry with no backward causal reference can contain mutual semantic opposition. **Construction.** Two available arguments conclude \(p\) and \(\neg p\); at later occurrences the inquirer records both directed rebuttals; both refer only to existing contents; precedence remains acyclic while opposition contains both directions. **Consequence.** Removing mutual opposition to preserve a chronological graph loses a legitimate situation.
439	
440	## Losing a premise loses an argument, not automatically its conclusion
441	
442	**Claim.** If an essential premise of \(u\) loses standing in appraisal \(j\), \(u\) is not usable in \(j\); the conclusion need not be false or unsupported by every other argument. **Derivation.** The universal clause of \(\mathrm{Usable}_j\) fails; a second argument without that dependence is unaffected; nothing establishes the negation. The consequence applies when \(u\) is a criticism; exempting criticisms would violate the condition.
443	
444	## Recursion is not universality
445	
446	**Counterexample.** An organization can conjecture about one subject, criticize those conjectures, and criticize its own standards within that subject, with arbitrarily many levels, while its organization prevents representation or critical learning of an independently specified \(p^\ast\) under every admitted enabling condition. The recursive condition holds while \(\mathrm{UU}\) or \(\mathrm{UC}\) fails at \(p^\ast\).
447	
448	## Recursion is not extensibility
449	
450	(FW2, from E1.) **Claim.** An organization can satisfy E0 and fail E1. **Construction.** Take the preceding counterexample and add that the constraint confining it is wired in: no content in \(K\) is such that withdrawing its standing widens the set of attempts. Then \(K^{\mathrm{gen}}\) does not contain the confining constraint as an eligible target. **Consequence.** The existing counterexample is a member of \(\mathrm{RecursiveCapacity}\setminus\mathrm{EX}\); what it lacks is not recursion but a constraint that is a content.
451	
452	## Provisional reasoning does not require a completed hierarchy of judges
453	
454	**Construction.** An investigator uses a provisional instrument model; a criticism identifies a vulnerability; a revised model is compared using other available explanations while unresolved assumptions are retained; the comparison changes the use of the original model. There is a finite episode with a genuine return from method criticism to object-level inquiry, and no premise has been justified for all purposes.
455	
456	## A finite record does not logically determine universal capacity
457	
458	**Claim.** A finite record of successful episodes, without organizational premises, does not entail \(\mathrm{UED}\). **Construction.** Two candidate models agree on the observed episodes; one admits a universal organization; the other has an unobserved barrier at an uncovered problem. Both fit. The conclusion is underdetermination by the record alone, not a ban on rationally accepting a universal explanation.
459	
460	## Explanation, creativity, and success do not collapse
461	
462	A person can invent a false account (\(\mathrm{OCA}\) without progress); a critic can respond to a real issue and introduce a worse theory (uptake without progress); a copier can transmit a correct explanation (possession without authorship); a learner can reconstruct an old explanation (newness and reconstructive authorship without historical firstness). None claims that copying, deduction, search, randomness, or communication is forbidden inside a creator.
463	
464	## General model learning is not explanatory organization
465	
466	(FW2, from A1.1.) **Claim.** An organization can satisfy a demanding set of conditions for general-purpose learning of predictive models while no interpretation in the base class assigns it any instance of \(\mathcal K\); it then lies outside the recursive-capacity class. **Construction.** Let \(s\) modify its models continuously, learn by moving its sensors, hold many complementary models of each object stored at locations in learned frames, and settle on a percept by consensus among them. Suppose its history contains no occurrence interpretable as a recognized difficulty, no content deployed as an account of one, and no occurrence alleging a defect with grounds and bearing. Then \(\mathrm{Attempt}\), \(\mathrm{Bearing}\), and \(\mathrm{UsesReason}\) have no instances and no instance of \(\mathcal K\) exists; \(s\) may nevertheless carry physical knowledge. **Consequence.** A checklist of learning attributes is a restrictive profile: passing it establishes general learning and not explanatory organization; failing it does not establish absence. The case sits between "Recursion is not universality" (an explainer confined to one subject) and the biological contrast (a lineage without criticism): an individual general learner with no explanatory activity. [H1]
467	
468	## A prediction error is not a criticism
469	
470	(FW2, from A1.2.) **Claim.** A mechanism that detects every mismatch between a model and its input and repairs the model does not instantiate reason-bearing criticism. **Construction.** Represent input, predictive state, mismatch event, and model change. To interpret it as \(c=\langle z,p,b,\delta,g,\lambda\rangle\), \(\delta\) would have to be a represented defect, \(g\) grounds, \(\lambda\) a bearing claim. The mismatch is an event; no bearing is represented; the response is fixed by the mechanism; the only variable in any contrast family is the presence of mismatch. **Consequence.** An expectation-and-surprise cycle is not the kernel; the disappointment of an inexplicit expectation becomes criticism only through an interpretation connecting it to an alleged error. The mechanism supplies enabling conditions for criticism, including evidence and attention; it is not criticism. [H1]
471	
472	## Consensus by suppression is not warrant
473	
474	(FW2, from A1.3.) **Claim.** A mechanism yielding one stable state from many partial models supplies no warrant, represents no appraisal, and produces determinations where the semantics permits none. **Construction.** Under one reading the mechanism intersects candidate sets; under another the common suppress the rare; under both the output is one state selected for action, and on a bistable input the mechanism picks. Elimination by joint constraint can be criticism when the constraints are contents represented as reasons; here nothing alleges a defect and the intersection is computed. Agreement among models is a count. On the bistable input the mechanism selects where "incomparability, disagreement about criteria, and unfinished assessment are permitted." **Consequence.** The strongest engineering case for a consensus mechanism, that it binds partial models into one percept and stabilizes it under moving sensors, is not epistemic. A theory taking convergence as warrant adopts a perceptual convenience as epistemology. The two readings must be kept apart because elimination by represented reasons can be criticism and majority suppression cannot. [H1]
475	
476	## Satisfying many constraints is a reason for preference, not a probability of truth
477	
478	(FW2, from A1.4.) **Claim.** An account meeting many independently discovered constraints may merit provisional preference without any probability of correctness being licensed. **Construction.** The crossword analogy: the more intersecting answers fit, the more certain the solution. A crossword has a finite grid, an answer key, and independent clues by construction; explanatory inquiry has none. \(\mathrm{FreeVariation}\) is comparative and respect-relative, and constraint is neither uniqueness nor truth certification. **Consequence.** The correct reading is that such an account does more explanatory work and is harder to vary; the incorrect reading is a confidence functional, which this theory does not have. [H1]
479	
480	## A reference frame is a background, and choosing one is a conjecture
481	
482	(FW2, from A1.5.) **Claim.** That the same facts arranged in different frames yield different conclusions is an instance of K-PROBLEM; a frame is a component of \(\xi\); choosing one is an explanatory act. **Construction.** Historical facts on a timeline suggest causal relations by temporal proximity; on a map, by spatial proximity; a good frame for an abstract subject may need dimensions nobody has named. In \(\xi\) a frame belongs to \(B\) and \(K\); a change of frame is a change to a material component and must be exposed. The description of a discovery as finding a better frame for the same facts misdescribes it: a new theory is a conjecture that can change what counts as a fact in the relevant respect. **Consequence.** The physical vocabulary of frames corroborates the theory; treating a frame as neutral scaffolding slides into inductivism, and K-CONJECTURE denies that arrangement supplies content. Lexical instances exist: one event admits alternative sparse schematizations licensing different constructions, neither recoverable from the scene's correlational texture. [H1; P2]
483	
484	## Blocking is not criticism
485	
486	(FW2, from A3.1.) **Claim.** Retreat from an overgenerated form on acquisition of a listed competitor for the same slot is first-layer competition among forms. **Construction.** A slot, two fillers, one attested; the attested suppresses the generated. Nothing represents a defect; the attested form is a competitor, not a reason; the outcome is fixed by attestation and slot uniqueness; the only variable is attestation. **Consequence.** Blocking is a correct policy for a conventional system, where attestation is the only ground there could be. It transfers to explanatory content only as a mistake: an account is not displaced by a competitor's being attested, repeated, or older. [P2]
487	
488	## Discarding is not criticism, and it marks the line between reconstruction and origination
489	
490	(FW2, from A3.2 and C2.2.) **Claim.** An organization that uses generated forms once and discards them, retaining only witnessed forms, corrects overgeneration without criticism; it can reconstruct and be productive; it cannot criticize what it generated and cannot originate. **Construction.** Productively formed entries are not listed; they are regenerated on demand; only witnessed forms are listed. Overgeneration is harmless because nothing generated enters the store with standing. The generator's products are never targets, since a target must be "already available for criticism." The organization can satisfy a domain-relative reconstruction attribution and can extend an inherited system; it cannot satisfy \(\mathrm{OCA}\) for its generated forms or an advance attributable to itself. **Consequence.** Reconstruction is compatible with a discard policy for generated candidates; origination is not. This is a retention-policy discriminator between \(\mathrm{UU}\)-type and \(\mathrm{UC}\)-type capacity at the level of the substrate, and it is why K-STANDING requires retention without standing rather than discarding. [P2]
491	
492	## Uptake is not criticism
493	
494	(FW2, from A3.3.) **Claim.** The process by which an innovation that violates current constraints becomes an actual form of a language over time is variation and selection at the cultural level. **Construction.** Many speakers generate possible forms; some are repeated; forms repeated enough become listed for the community. No speaker represents a defect in a rejected form or a reason for an adopted one. Substitute forms for variants and uptake for reproduction in the biological contrast; it applies unchanged. **Consequence.** Language change by uptake is real and is a source of novelty; it is reason-free and outside the kernel, and it is the mechanism by which false models spread when what spreads is a belief. [P2; H1]
495	
496	## Reconstruction is not extensibility
497	
498	(FW2, from E1.) **Claim.** An organization can extend into a new domain without satisfying E0. **Construction.** The reconstructing learner acquires a second inherited system from positive evidence by the same generator and acceptance policy; its repertoire now covers a subject it did not; no instance of \(\mathcal K\) occurred. **Consequence.** Extension of repertoire is not extension in the sense of E2, which requires \(\mathrm{UnderstandAndCriticize}\) and \(\mathrm{CreativeCriticalAdvance}\); the first-layer class can grow without entering \(\mathrm{EX}\).
499	
500	## Extension by replacement is not extension
501	
502	(FW2, from E1.) **Claim.** An organization can come to satisfy E2 for some \(D^\ast\) by a change that fails E3. **Construction.** A designer adds a new sensor modality and its learning modules to a modular sensorimotor system, or an operator adds a new collection to an organization of language models under a host. The composite now learns, and with additions may criticize, in the new domain. The route was the designer's act, not a criticism by the organization of a constraint in its own \(K^{\mathrm{gen}}\). **Consequence.** Membership in \(\mathrm{EX}\) is established only by an extension the organization brings about itself, traceably; enlargement of \(\chi\) is admissible, but the extension must be the organization's. [H5; H6]
503	
504	## The organization of language models under a host
505	
506	(FW2, from E1, Case 4.) **Claim.** A composite of language-model participants under a deterministic host that retains contributions as targets without standing, separates examination from adoption, records dependencies and case descriptions over uses, and enacts mediated use changes is a candidate for the recursive-capacity class; it fails E1 as constituted, for a specific and repairable reason. **Construction.** The constraints determining which contents a participant can deploy as attempts are its weights and training. Within a run these have no standing the organization can withdraw; they are not contents in the composite's \(K\). The host's revisable attention methods constrain selection and supply, not generation. So \(K^{\mathrm{gen}}\) for the composite contains constraints that are not eligible targets. **Consequence.** The composite is at most in \(\mathrm{RecursiveCapacity}\) and a specification adopting this authority should not claim more for it. Repair requires that the organization be able to represent, criticize, and change what its participants can conjecture, within the run and traceably; adjustment by the operator between runs is extension by replacement. Whether an organization with frozen generators can satisfy E2 through E1-satisfying constraints elsewhere in \(K\) is an open question.
507	
508	## The combinatorial medium is a realization constraint
509	
510	(FW2, from C1.1.) **Claim.** Any realization of an organization in the recursive-capacity class must support individuals distinct from kinds, composition, binding across roles, and embedding to unbounded depth. **Construction.** A complete critical episode contains \(z\), \(c\) about \(z\), and \(\alpha\) with \(\mathrm{UsesReason}\); target closure allows \(c'\) about \(c\); role preservation gives \(c'\) the same structure. Representing \(c\) requires identifying \(z\) as a particular content bound to two roles; representing \(c'\) requires embedding \(c\) as a target; representing \(\mathrm{UsesReason}\) requires identifying the same \(c\) across \(\mathfrak C\). An organization whose states cannot do these cannot instantiate target closure as a capacity. **Consequence.** A constraint on \(\Theta\) modules, not on the semantics; stated without a substrate; more general than any proposal about symbols, frames, or networks. [P1]
511	
512	## Cognitive closure is a well-formed criticism of an attribution, not of the class
513	
514	(FW2, from C1.2.) **Claim.** The proposal that a human mind is constitutionally unable to solve certain problems because they do not decompose combinatorially is a criticism of the attribution of \(\mathrm{UED}\) to humans; it is compatible with the class definition; the authority fixes what a reply must show. **Construction.** The proposal characterizes a domain \(D^{\ast\ast}\) independently of human successes, asserts an organizational barrier, concedes the barrier is a property of one organ of one species so that a universal explainer is coherent, and states a refutation condition. This is the form a challenge must take. In the stratified hierarchy it is the claim \(s\in\mathrm{EX}\setminus\mathrm{UED}\). **Consequence.** Three obligations bind any reply and any defense. A record of failure is not a barrier; the argument must be organizational. The attribution is to the continuing organization under admissible enabling conditions including external representation and tools, so claims about the unaided organ do not engage it, while the claim that a supplied solution could not be understood does. The problem formulations in \(D^{\ast\ast}\) are themselves criticizable, so a demonstration of closure must show that no admissible reformulation dissolves them, and a defense by reformulation must show the difficulty is preserved. [P1; B3; B6]
515	
516	## Evolved constraints on generalization are provisional background, not warrant
517	
518	(FW2, from C1.3.) **Claim.** An organism's evolved constraints on similarity and generalization are contents with \(\mathrm{Standing}\), deployable as background and withdrawable under criticism; they supply no inductive warrant. **Construction.** A lineage instantiates physical knowledge without representing a problem or a reason; the constraint is present as an inherited disposition; when it contributes to a judgment it occupies the role of a background content \(d\) with \(\mathrm{Standing}_j(d;u)\); it can be wrong for the case and withdrawn, and the generalization it licensed then loses that application. **Consequence.** Inborn expectations are prior conjectures, which is all K-CONJECTURE needs and all this theory grants. A similarity space supplies no grain; a promotion of similarity to identity must state one.
519	
520	## The no-negative-evidence constraint
521	
522	(FW2, from C2.2.) **Claim.** An organization reconstructing an open-ended target from positive evidence alone cannot use evidential refutation against overgenerating conjectures; it must have a constrained generator, endogenous withdrawal, or a distinction between formation and acceptance. **Construction.** A superset conjecture is compatible with every positive datum, so no datum bears on it as criticism and \(\mathrm{Bearing}\) has no instance. A learner that nevertheless arrives at the exclusions does so by denying standing to generated forms, listing only witnessed ones, and letting development be the acquisition of more accurate meanings rather than the narrowing of a rule. **Consequence.** K-STANDING is what makes generation safe under positive evidence; the constraint is substrate-independent. [P2]
523	
524	## The learnability-universality tension
525	
526	(FW2, from C2.3.) **Claim.** Constraints on a generator that make reconstruction from positive evidence possible are, if fixed, parochial barriers; an organization claimed to be universal must hold them as contents in \(K\), eligible for the kernel and withdrawable. **Construction.** The first horn of the no-negative-evidence problem is a constrained generator. A fixed constraint is the counterexample "Recursion is not universality." K-RECURSION requires that methods be criticizable with effect on operative use; the constraints that make a domain learnable are methods in that sense once they are contents. Revision at the community level over history, by innovation and uptake, is variation and selection and is not the kernel. **Consequence.** An attribution of universality to a learnable organization must show that its generator constraints are revisable within the continuing organization under admissible \(\chi\); tools, notation, and metalinguistic knowledge are what convert a constrained generator into one whose constraints have standing. This is E1 of the extensible class, seen from the learner's side. [P2]
527	
528	## A worked inquiry: two balances and a changing question
529	
530	A stipulated thought experiment. An object is placed on two balances reading 10 and 12. The investigator trusts the second and proposes the first reads low. A colleague asks why the second is trusted; if only because its reading agrees with the proposed mass, the account uses its conclusion to select its standard, and the problem becomes what licenses treating either as reference. Suppose constant additive offsets: \(m_A=x+b_A\), \(m_B=x+b_B\), with \(10=x+b_A\), \(12=x+b_B\). Both \((12,-2,0)\) and \((10,0,2)\) fit, and for any \(\lambda\), \((x+\lambda,b_A-\lambda,b_B-\lambda)\) leaves both readings unchanged: the readings determine \(b_B-b_A=2\), not \(x\). Repetition does not remove the ambiguity; an independently relevant constraint is needed. The useful result is a better problem situation, not a certified mass. The subsidiary result is criticizable (offsets may not be constant); a later calibration certificate is evidence only through an account of what was calibrated and why it applies, and a criticism of applicability affects the argument using it whichever side it serves. A collaborator's discovery of the invariance while the investigator repeats the result yields a different attribution from the investigator's own reconstruction.
531	
532	## Explanatory constraint and reach without a list of outputs
533	
534	Deutsch's seasons example: axial orientation, orbital relations, and illumination geometry constrain the account; substituting an agent's mood does not preserve the work. The explanation applies beyond the locations considered because of what it says. Its reach must still be stated accurately; discovering the need for a further explanation is the next problem, not a reason to conceal the distinction. [B1]
535	
536	## Inexplicit and artistic inquiry
537	
538	An artist can recognize that a passage does not achieve an intended effect, vary it, and distinguish improvement from irrelevant alteration without an explicit theory. The burden is to explain that discrimination and its use, not to require a prior formal specification; a claim that the work discovers objective aesthetic knowledge requires the further aesthetic interpretation. [B14]
539	
540	## Distributed inquiry and biological contrast
541	
542	In a collaboration, one may identify the problem, another invent a candidate, a third expose a defect, and the group preserve a revision; a system-level attribution requires the causal connections and shared use that make these one inquiry. Agreement or membership alone is not such a connection. A biological lineage can acquire an adaptation through heritable variation and differential reproduction without representing the difficulty as a problem or proposing a reason against a variant; it instantiates physical knowledge without explanatory criticism. Blind lower-level variation does not eliminate the explanatory significance of higher-level thought. [F3; M5]
543

545	
546	# Part IV. Adequacy, scope, and remaining questions
547	
548	## What an application must explain
549	
550	A proposed application must identify the system and boundary, the represented difficulty, the relevant content, and the causal organization of the contribution. Where criticism is claimed it must explain bearing and uptake; where progress, the improvement; where recursive capacity, how scrutiny affects operative methods; where extensibility, which generator constraint was criticized, how its standing changed, and what the change effected; where universality, the domain, enabling conditions, continuity, and capacity clauses directly. No transcript of a mind is required; no certificate format is required; no absence in an archive settles a claim about everything the system could do.
551	
552	## What would count against the theory
553	
554	The explanation-centered core would be challenged by a defensible account of explanatory knowledge creation with no problem-directed conjectural or critical organization at the relevant level. The reason-use analysis would need revision if it excluded genuine understanding or included content-insensitive compliance after the causal differences were made explicit. The recursive account would be inadequate if it allowed an operative standard to remain immune while claiming criticism had effect, or required a final evaluator for local progress. The transport account would fail if it disconnected legitimate revolutions or admitted arbitrary changes as solutions. The universality conditions would need revision if their resource clauses covertly supplied every achievement, if their domains were selected by successes, or if the understanding-creating distinction misdescribed universal ability. An attribution of \(\mathrm{UED}\) would be challenged by a genuine organizational barrier to an independently characterized domain under enabling conditions that do not remove the barrier by replacing the system.
555	
556	**K-STANDING** would need revision if a defensible account of self-criticism were found in an organization that grants standing on generation or discards what it generates, or if the distinction between retention and standing could not be applied to any realization without a theory of mechanism. **The extensible class** would need withdrawal if E1 could not be stated without a mechanistic notion of a generator, if E1 turned out to be entailed by target closure after all, or if E2 and E3 added nothing to domain-relative \(\mathrm{UED}\) as already reported. (FW2.)
557	
558	Renaming an inconvenient case, changing scope silently, or declaring every negative case "not a real problem" would not answer any of these.
559	
560	## Named criticism routes and conjectures
561	
562	(FW2, new.) A commitment that names its strongest published opponent is more contestable than one that does not.
563	
564	**Cognitive closure.** The named challenge to the attribution of \(\mathrm{UED}\) to humans is the proposal that problems lacking part-whole and lawful-relation structure are constitutionally beyond a combinatorial mind. It concedes the coherence of the universal class and contests membership; in this theory's terms it asserts that humans are in \(\mathrm{EX}\setminus\mathrm{UED}\). Its obligations are stated in Part III. Its published counter-argument is that any explanation comprehensible to a universal explainer is comprehensible to a person, so closure would require that the barred problems have no explanation; that argument is itself a conjecture about reach and is eligible for criticism on the same terms. [P1; B3; B6]
565	
566	**The jump conjecture.** \(\mathrm{EX}_{\Theta,\beta}=\mathrm{UED}_{\Theta,\beta}\): an organization that has extended itself into one independently specified domain by criticizing and revising its own generator constraints, traceably, has the capacity to do so for any admitted domain, the remaining differences between domains being differences in \(\chi\). This is this theory's form of the claim that universality arrives as a jump. It is refuted by an organization shown to be in \(\mathrm{EX}\) and shown, by an organizational argument meeting the closure obligations, to be barred from some domain. If it holds, the extensible class is not proper on that side and its value is to name the condition that makes the jump possible; if it fails, closure has a member. [B6]
567	
568	**Two layers of error correction.** Any physical realization of the kernel contains a fidelity-correcting layer over representations and a content-correcting layer over contents, the second not obtainable by iterating the first. This is refuted by an organization with a single error-correcting layer that instantiates the kernel, or by evidence that content-level criticism co-varies strictly with representational stability so that no dissociation can be produced. The research program that tests it is external to this authority. [H1; CT1]
569	
570	## What is and is not established
571	
572	The theory supplies a recursive organization of semantic roles, an explicit universal target class, a stratified hierarchy between recursion and universality, and distinctions that prevent false identifications: history with judgment, criticism with rejection, understanding with transmission, explanatory progress with persistence, recursion with universality, recursion with extensibility, productivity with creativity, general learning with explanatory organization, consensus with warrant, and physical task capacity with creativity.
573	
574	It does not derive the existence of an actual universal explainer from definitions. It does not give a complete reductive account of explanation, meaning, causal authorship, progress, or creative capacity. The constructions make additional commitments explicit; their success must be assessed by the explanations they support and the criticisms they survive. The remaining question is explanatory: what organization makes the attributed capacities possible, how do its parts do the claimed work, and why do the distinctions hold. The same kernel applies to attempts to answer it.
575	
576	## Refinement without semantic substitution
577	
578	A specification adopting this theory distinguishes a **semantic assertion**, an **attribution judgment**, a **record fact**, and a **machine-check result**. A machine may check that a document has required fields, that a finite derivation uses stated premises, that a counterfactual experiment met a stated comparison, or that a content's own stated operands satisfy a relation it asserts. None of these establishes that its interpretation of explanation, reason use, authorship, progress, or capacity is correct.
579	
580	Let \(A\) be the interpretation of this authority and \(D\) a dossier or implementation state. A refinement provides a partial interpretation relation \(\mathcal I(D,A)\), not a definition of \(A\) as whatever the implementation accepts. For every projected claim it states subject, scope, interpretation, dependencies, and whether the projection concerns a record fact, a situated judgment, or semantic satisfaction. A machine-level classification may entail a semantic proposition only under an explicit bridge whose adequacy is open to criticism. A restrictive profile can require an explicit graph, an intervention family, a finite event vocabulary, or a witness format; failure to satisfy it is failure of that check, not absence of the phenomenon; passing it is not a definition. The connection must be substantive in both directions and must test legitimate cases against unintended exclusion: inherited targets, communicated reconstruction, inexplicit contributions, method change, nonreplacement results, provisional closure.
581	
582	Admission, use, and truth are distinct (K-STANDING). Recording a proposed case does not make its body satisfy its checks; satisfying checks does not make premises true; a mechanically failed body must not be reported as passed because nobody objected. Noninductivism forbids manufacturing warrant from a count of endorsements or repetitions, from agreement among instances or components, from attestation, or from a count of satisfied constraints; it does not make different arguments or new information irrelevant because they share a conclusion. Operational stopping and epistemic immunity are different. A specification may itself be criticized through the inquiry it supports; a replacement can be enacted by a person, institution, or mechanism without a self-rewriting evaluator, and the account must identify the criticism, replacement, decision, and effects. Version labels establish traceability, not return relevance.
583	
584	## Further discriminating cases
585	
586	**Delayed reconstruction.** A relay emits a received explanation at \(e_1\) without reconstructing it; the system develops the understanding at \(e_2\). Authorship at \(e_2\) cannot combine with novelty and attempted use at \(e_1\) to establish \(\mathrm{OCA}\) at \(e_1\).
587	
588	**Inherited target, original criticism.** An investigator inherits a theory, notices a defect, and creates an explanation of it. A creative critical episode is possible though the investigator did not originate the theory and the new explanation is not its descendant; a definition requiring lineage excludes this.
589	
590	**Ordinary premise under criticism.** A criticism depends essentially on an observation interpretation rather than a labeled standard; withdrawing it removes that application's support without refuting the criticism's conclusion or reinstating the theory.
591	
592	**Same target, different achievement.** A tutor supplies a complete explanation and the learner reconstructs it; this creates knowledge for the learner without establishing the capacity to originate it under an achievement condition excluding a supplied solution.
593	
594	**One system, two boundaries.** (FW2.) A person's grammar-acquisition subsystem is in the first-layer class: it reconstructs an inherited system from positive evidence, denies standing to what it generates, and instantiates no kernel. The person, at the boundary that includes notation, explicit grammar, and communication, is a candidate for the extensible class. Attributions are made at boundaries; the same physical system can host members of different classes at different \(\beta\).
595	
596	---
597	
598	# Research program (external to the authority)
599	
600	The program that tests the two-layer conjecture, the retention discriminator, and the realization constraints against a settling substrate and against an organization of language models under a host is stated in addendum A2 (hash above) and is not part of the semantics. Its products enter this authority only as constraints on \(\Theta\) modules in the manner of the realization section, and only after audit.
601	
602	---
603	
604	# Source keys and attribution boundaries
605	
606	**F1 - David Deutsch, *The Fabric of Reality*.** Chapter 1, printed pages 2 to 13 and 19 to 28. Explanation versus prediction, creative subsidiary explanation, autonomous higher-level explanation.
607	
608	**F3 - David Deutsch, *The Fabric of Reality*.** Chapter 3, printed pages 59 to 70, principally 67 to 68. Anti-inductivism, problem-directed conjecture and criticism, recursive subsidiary inquiry, the comparison with biological evolution.
609	
610	**B1 - David Deutsch, *The Beginning of Infinity* (2011).** Chapter 1, printed pages 24 to 32. Explanatory constraint, reach, rules of thumb.
611	
612	**B3 - David Deutsch, *The Beginning of Infinity*.** Chapter 3, "The Spark." People as universal explainers; explanatory reach not bounded by the explainer's origins. (FW2: added for the closure counter-argument.)
613	
614	**B6 - David Deutsch, *The Beginning of Infinity*.** Chapter 6, printed pages 145 to 147. The jump to universality; existing reach versus historical use. The UU/UC/UED decomposition and the extensible class are modeling proposals, not Deutsch's formulas.
615	
616	**B7 - David Deutsch, *The Beginning of Infinity*.** Chapter 7, printed pages 155 to 157. Explanatory attribution of the origin of knowledge; insufficiency of a behavior-only criterion.
617	
618	**B14 - David Deutsch, *The Beginning of Infinity*.** Chapter 14, printed pages 364 to 368. Inexplicit explanatory knowledge; the objective-aesthetics proposal.
619	
620	**B16 - David Deutsch, *The Beginning of Infinity*.** Chapter 16, printed pages 411 to 415. Creative reconstruction in transmission.
621	
622	**M5 - Chiara Marletto, *The Science of Can and Can't* (2021).** Chapter 5. Generalized and abstract catalysts; information contributing to its own preservation.
623	
624	**M7 - Chiara Marletto, *The Science of Can and Can't*.** Chapter 7. Counterfactual knowledge; creativity as knowledge creation by thinking.
625	
626	**CT1 - David Deutsch and Chiara Marletto, "Constructor theory of information," *Proceedings of the Royal Society A* (2015).** Information media; copying and distinguishability; error correction as a condition of retained capacity. (FW2.)
627	
628	**H1 - Jeff Hawkins, *A Thousand Brains* (2021).** Chapters 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, and 12 to 16. Used for contrast cases and as a candidate \(\Theta\) module; the extension of reference frames to conceptual knowledge is, by its author's statement, speculative. Not adopted. (FW2.)
629	
630	**H2 - Hawkins, Lewis, Klukas, Purdy, Ahmad, "A Framework for Intelligence and Cortical Function Based on Grid Cells in the Neocortex," *Frontiers in Neural Circuits* 12 (2019).** Primary statement of the frames-and-columns account. (FW2.)
631	
632	**H5, H6 - Clay, Leadholm, Hawkins, "The Thousand Brains Project" (2024); Leadholm et al., "Thousand-Brains Systems," *Neural Computation* (2025).** The open implementation used in the extension-by-replacement case. (FW2.)
633	
634	**P1 - Steven Pinker, *How the Mind Works* (1997).** Chapter 2 for the combinatorial medium; chapter 8, final section, for cognitive closure. The evolutionary psychology and the correlational account of information are not adopted. (FW2.)
635	
636	**P2 - Steven Pinker, *Learnability and Cognition*, new edition (2013; first 1989).** Chapter 1 for the logical problem and Baker's paradox; chapter 4 for possible and actual forms; chapter 7 for the unlearning problem and listedness; chapter 8 for the resolution and spatial schemas. The linguistic analyses are not adopted; the property-/existence-predicting distinction is J. D. Fodor's as the source states. (FW2.)
637	
638	**Attribution boundary.** The distinctions in this document are its own. The sources marked (FW2) supplied mechanisms, positions, and worked domains against which those distinctions are exhibited; none proposes this theory or its classes, and none is committed to them.
639	
640	---

---

## A recursive semantic theory of explanatory knowledge and universal explanatory capacity, with a stratified class hierarchy and realization constraints

### Purpose and standing

The subject of this theory is how a system can create explanations, expose errors in them, and change the problems, standards, and methods through which it does that. Its target is **explanatory universality**: an organization whose explanatory reach is not permanently confined to a predetermined subject matter, vocabulary, repertoire of answers, or hierarchy of judges.

The kernel is recursive. Recognizing a problem can itself present a problem. Inventing a conjecture, understanding a criticism, interpreting an observation, choosing between explanations, or deciding whether a standard is appropriate can each require the same process of conjecture and criticism. The process can return to any of those activities without installing a final authority above them. This is the substantive structure described in *The Fabric of Reality*, chapter 3, particularly printed pages 67 to 68. [F3]

This is a semantic theory, not an execution procedure. No algorithm for generating explanations, computing verdicts, recognizing every error, or completing an inquiry is required. Whether a particular physical realization is computable is neither a premise nor a conclusion. Recursive self-application must not be reduced to a computational fixed point, and it does not, merely by being recursive, establish a mathematical uncomputability result.

**Standing.** This document is a candidate successor to *FW1a* (SHA-256 `823f508867d779cbea9b8f878d876dab94d635b97bdb17512942a2ac9619e41e`). It is canonical for any specification that explicitly adopts FW2. FW1a remains the authority for specifications that adopt it; supersession is by adoption, not by fiat. Authority fixes the meanings against which a specification is assessed; it does not confer immunity from criticism on the theory.

**What FW2 adds to 1.0.** One core commitment (K-STANDING), stated because the learnability analysis showed it is what makes conjecture safe and the retention analysis showed it marks the line between reconstruction and origination. One class in the capacity hierarchy (the extensible class) and one comparison class outside it (the first-layer class), because the step from recursion to universality in FW1a had one counterexample and no articulated structure. A realization section that states substrate-independent constraints on any physical realization of the recursive-capacity class. Seventeen discriminating cases added to Part III. A named criticism route (cognitive closure) and a named conjecture (the jump conjecture) in Part IV. Extended source keys. Nothing in FW1a is withdrawn.

**Provenance and change register.** The additions were developed in six addenda to FW1a, hashed as follows, and are integrated here with their derivations compressed. An audit of FW2 against FW1a should use the register in the closing section.

- A1 `cd251bcf4c25628eab929714e1de2b2e76c34412e89300f505309dd682c6b4a8` contrast cases from a predictive-model account of intelligence
- A2 `9d55a329b1012d6ee3ce4b5a0b5aeb3c796df7c931f7207bf02bdbf9419db8a7` research program: explanation from consensus
- A3 `779e9f5c2c588611fe6f6e1cdde8aaea717e2781b35305dd2a1ef46f2f451169` blocking, discarding, uptake; retention
- C1 `a946766536678c2afb65b15e9fe7d7d101608c1050fcba918166c1747d82cc47` combinatorial medium; cognitive closure
- C2 `3cf5bf6a9d66889e7db64b984d100a6036543ee24acf5f19ddf7e13b9a128a55` learnability; standing of generated forms
- E1 `0183388193b28c9aa02c88052506102df0118b5c37b91327de00ce56ed3bb57f` the extensible class

The title names a proposed Popperian reconstruction, informed by Deutsch and Marletto. It does not attribute the theory to any of them. Source-backed commitments, additional modeling commitments, definitions, and derived consequences are distinguished throughout. Source keys are resolved at the end.

---

# Part I-A. The explanatory core

## Reality is not conferred by a judgment (K-REAL)

An explanation attempts to say how something is, works, or follows from a structure, and why the relevant phenomenon or relation has the character it does. Its content is not exhausted by the observations it fits, the responses it produces, or the approval it receives. A represented explanation, an agent's assessment of it, and what it actually explains are different things. This distinction applies to an assessment of the present theory as much as to any other. [F1; B1]

Errors can be real when nobody has identified them. An objection can be mistaken when nobody has answered it. No authority, procedure, record, tradition, or successful history turns a fallible judgment into a guarantee. Fallibility does not imply that all explanations are equally good or that knowledge is impossible; it means that explanatory improvement is not final certification. [F3; B1]

## A problem is an interpreted difficulty that matters (K-PROBLEM)

An active problem arises when a system recognizes a tension, inadequacy, or unresolved relation among ideas and directs attention to it as worth addressing. The difficulty may be inexplicit. It need not be a contradiction, an anomaly, or an emergency; a wish to understand more deeply can be enough. Recognition and values affect which difficulty receives attention; neither makes the recognized difficulty automatically genuine. [F3; B1]

The world does not supply a ready-made partition into the problems a thinker must solve. Background explanations, recognition, purposes, and standards contribute to that partition, and each can subsequently become problematic. Attention therefore belongs inside the theory rather than being an unexplained selector outside it. A frame in which facts are arranged is such a background: the same facts arranged differently yield different difficulties and different conclusions, and the choice of arrangement carries content and is itself criticizable. (FW2: the last sentence, from A1.5 and C2.5.)

## Conjecture precedes criticism of that conjecture (K-CONJECTURE)

A conjecture supplies a proposed content, interpretation, or organization to criticize. It need not be justified before it is entertained. Observation may occasion its invention and existing knowledge may contribute to it, but neither repetition nor deduction from observational instances supplies the missing explanatory content by itself. [F3; B1]

The order is a dependence of roles: criticism has something it criticizes. It is not a requirement that every conjecture be written out before a difficulty can be noticed. An inexplicit expectation can be the prior conjecture. A criticism is also conjectural content; once proposed, it too can be criticized. "Conjecture before criticism" does not appoint an uncriticizable first conjecture.

## Criticism has a reason-bearing role (K-CRITICISM)

Criticism proposes that some content, inference, application, standard, or practice has a defect relevant to a problem. A reason-sensitive response depends on what the objection says and on how the alleged defect bears on the problem. Negative feedback, punishment, disagreement, failure, or rejection is not criticism merely because it changes behavior. Such events can become evidentially significant through an interpretation that connects them to a conjecture and an alleged error. [F3; B7]

A response may improve an explanation, reject it, retain it against an objection, investigate further, reinterpret evidence, alter a standard, reframe the problem, or suspend judgment. It can also be mistaken. The semantic role of a critical response and its epistemic success must remain separate. (FW2: three mechanisms that resemble criticism and are not it are fixed in Part III: a prediction-error signal that repairs a model, suppression of a candidate by an attested competitor, and settlement among partial models. Each changes behavior; none represents a defect with grounds and bearing.)

## The same kernel applies to its own working parts (K-RECURSION)

Anything doing explanatory or adjudicative work is eligible to become the subject of further conjecture and criticism: a problem formulation, a criticism, the interpretation of a reason, an inferential connection, an observation model, a comparison, a novelty attribution, a system boundary, a stopping decision, an evidential practice, and the methods being used to assess them. [F3]

Recursive scrutiny must be able to matter. A criticism of a standard can change how arguments using that standard are assessed; a criticism of an interpretation can change what an earlier utterance is taken to have said; a criticism of an attribution boundary can change who receives credit. Merely allowing comments about a method while permanently insulating its consequences would not satisfy this commitment.

Recursion does not require an infinite chain of prior authorizations. A system can reason provisionally with its present resources while examining a particular part of them, suspend the examination, act under a qualified judgment, or discover a better starting point. No requirement to solve every subsidiary problem first is imposed. On the realization side the same point is forced: no organization consults rules all the way down, so at some point a rule is executed rather than consulted, and provisional reasoning is both semantically legitimate and physically necessary. (FW2: the last sentence, from C1.5.)

## Generation confers no standing (K-STANDING)

(FW2, new.) A content's being generated by a system, whether by conjecture, by a lawful rule, or by any other route, confers no standing on it: it is not thereby available as a premise, an endorsed account, or an actual form. Standing is conferred by an appraisal in a specified respect, and the appraisal is itself content eligible for the kernel. Conversely, denial of standing is not deletion: a generated content may be retained as an occurrence available for criticism while having no standing in any application.

This commitment is stated separately because it is what makes conjecture safe and criticism possible. It makes conjecture safe because an organization that generates freely but grants nothing standing by generation can overgenerate without harm; this is how a learner reconstructs an open-ended target from positive evidence alone, where no datum can refute a superset conjecture. It makes criticism possible because a conjecture must be retained as a target while a rival is in use; an organization that either grants standing on generation or discards what it generates has no such target. Admission to a collection, use in an argument application, and truth are three things, and the kernel lives in the distinction. [P2; from C2.2 and A3.2]

## Creation has a provenance; understanding can be reconstructive (K-ORIGIN)

Attribution of creativity concerns the production or reconstruction of problem-specific explanatory organization, not the emission of an unfamiliar token. A prior explanation can contribute to a new creative act. A learner can reconstruct an explanation that exists elsewhere without having possessed it beforehand. A group can create through contributions that no isolated participant supplies in full. [F1; B7; B16]

Newness, authorship, understanding, correctness, and historical priority are distinct. A communicated explanation is not automatically a disqualification, and absence of a communicated complete answer is not automatically proof of authorship. Most originative acts are small at the relevant grain; an act need not be large to be one. (FW2: the last sentence, from C1.5.)

## Knowledge growth is explanatory improvement, not persistence (K-PROGRESS)

Successful explanatory knowledge creation requires an actual improvement in the relevant problem situation through explanatory work and error correction. A new conjecture need not achieve it; a critical response need not; retention alone does not. Improvement need not consist in a replacement theory: exposing a defective question, correcting a standard, or establishing a principled limitation can improve the situation. [F3]

The resulting knowledge remains fallible and can generate new problems. Improvement is assessed with its scope and dependencies visible. Changing the standard to declare victory does not establish improvement; neither does requiring every old commitment to survive. Improvement has no global direction and no terminus: a later theory may replace an earlier one by transport rather than incorporation, and no stage is one at which everything is known. (FW2: the last sentence, from A1.6.)

## Universality is a capacity claim, not a collection of successful episodes (K-UNIVERSALITY)

The target universal class contains systems capable, under suitable non-question-begging enabling conditions, of understanding explanations and conducting creative, critical inquiry across explanatory subject matters without a fixed parochial barrier. The capacity includes extending the represented vocabulary, revising problem formulations, revising the constraints on what the system can conjecture, and improving the methods needed for unfamiliar domains. [B6; B7; B16] (FW2: "revising the constraints on what the system can conjecture," from C2.3 and E1.)

This is stronger than an ability to repeat criticism, than performance across a large finite menu, and than permission to discuss anything. It is different from already knowing everything, succeeding on every attempt, solving a physically impossible demand, possessing unlimited resources now, or surviving indefinitely. Its formal obligations appear in Part II and are constitutive of the universal class.

K-UNIVERSALITY is an explicit substantive target commitment, not derived from K-RECURSION. Whether a particular system possesses the capacity requires an explanatory account of its organization; a finite performance record does not settle the question, in either direction. A checklist of learning attributes, however general the learning, does not settle it either: a system can learn continuously, by movement, with many complementary models and general representational frames, and instantiate no explanatory activity. (FW2: the last sentence, from A1.1.)

## Physical embodiment constrains without replacing explanation (K-PHYSICALITY)

When this theory is applied to an actual system, its contents and activities must have a physically tenable realization. Physical embodiment does not make semantic organization dispensable. An account of particle trajectories and an account of why a theory was revised answer different questions, although they must be compatible. [F1]

Constructor theory contributes a language of possible and impossible transformations, information-bearing substrates, and retained capacities. It does not, just by calling a process a constructor, explain the origin of its knowledge or the meaning of its representations. Physical knowledge that contributes to its own preservation and explanatory knowledge that improves understanding are related but nonidentical. [M5; M7] Part II states what any realization of the recursive-capacity class must be able to do, without naming a substrate. (FW2: the last sentence.)

# Part I-B. Why the independent commitments are needed

The following explain why these commitments are adopted and which distinctions would be lost without them. They are not claims of ultimate justification, nor proofs that no alternative formalism could use a different primitive vocabulary. A commitment is independent when it is not supplied by the other displayed definitions and must be stated rather than smuggled into a theorem.

**Explanatory realism cannot be supplied by a record of endorsements.** Two communities can endorse the same sentence for different reasons, or endorse incompatible sentences. Recording endorsements determines what they accepted, not which account explains the phenomenon. Omitting K-REAL permits a model in which "good explanation" means "accepted by the selected judge." Realism provides the distinction between being judged adequate and being adequate; it provides no infallible test. [F1; B1]

**Problem recognition cannot be supplied by an external task label.** A thermostat, a student, and an investigator can be exposed to the same reading. Calling the input a "problem" does not establish that each recognizes a difficulty. K-PROBLEM requires an interpretation of the role the discrepancy plays for the system, and values explain why attention goes to this difficulty rather than others. [F3]

**Conjectural origin is not a consequence of causal dependence on data.** A system may causally depend on observations without extracting an explanation from them. K-CONJECTURE prevents a causal input relation from becoming an undeclared rule of epistemic instruction, leaving room for observation, deduction, analogy, imagination, and inherited knowledge to participate without any of them being an automatic source of warrant. [F3; B1]

**Criticism is not supplied by variation and selection alone.** Differential persistence can occur without a represented objection, and a person can understand an objection and decide, for reasons, not to change. K-CRITICISM adds a content-sensitive relation not recoverable by counting revisions or outputs. A declaration that a signal was a reason is insufficient. [F3; B7]

**Recursion is stronger than maintaining an attackable archive.** An archive can contain criticism of a standard while the institution continues to apply it unconditionally. K-RECURSION requires a possible return from scrutiny to the operative use of the target and blocks a fixed hierarchy in which the final judge's judgments can never acquire a defect. [F3]

**Standing is not supplied by conjecture or by criticism.** (FW2, new.) K-CONJECTURE says criticism has something to criticize; it does not say that what is generated lacks standing. K-CRITICISM says what a criticism is; it does not say that its target must be retained. A theory with both and without K-STANDING permits two organizations it should distinguish: one that grants standing on generation, so that every conjecture is an endorsement and overgeneration is error; and one that discards its conjectures on use, so that nothing it generates is ever a target. The first cannot learn safely; the second cannot criticize itself. Both are excluded by the one commitment. [P2]

**Provenance is not supplied by output quality.** An answer can be accurate because its organization was created by the system, supplied by a collaborator, or retrieved from a store. K-ORIGIN locates the contribution rather than inferring it from surface quality or excluding it from a transmission history. [B7; B16]

**Improvement is not supplied by either change or retention.** Changing a theory may make it worse; retaining one may preserve an error; removing a local defect can damage the explanation elsewhere. K-PROGRESS adds the relation between the contribution and the whole relevant problem situation. [F3]

**Universality is not supplied by unrestricted self-reference.** A system might examine its standards indefinitely while confined to one kind of puzzle; another might name every discipline and learn none. K-UNIVERSALITY requires explanatory capacity across an independently specified domain, not reflective vocabulary. Nor is it supplied by general learning, however continuous or flexible, since learning a model of the world is not explaining it. [B6; B7] (FW2: last sentence.)

**Physical realization is not supplied by abstract consistency.** A coherent description of a capacity need not be realizable; reliable physical transformation does not establish semantic authorship. K-PHYSICALITY supplies the realization question and prevents either inference. [M5; M7]
