# Part IV. Adequacy, scope, and remaining questions

## What an application must explain

A proposed application must identify the system and boundary, the represented difficulty, the relevant content, and the causal organization of the contribution. Where criticism is claimed it must explain bearing and uptake; where progress, the improvement; where recursive capacity, how scrutiny affects operative methods; where extensibility, which generator constraint was criticized, how its standing changed, and what the change effected; where universality, the domain, enabling conditions, continuity, and capacity clauses directly. No transcript of a mind is required; no certificate format is required; no absence in an archive settles a claim about everything the system could do.

## What would count against the theory

The explanation-centered core would be challenged by a defensible account of explanatory knowledge creation with no problem-directed conjectural or critical organization at the relevant level. The reason-use analysis would need revision if it excluded genuine understanding or included content-insensitive compliance after the causal differences were made explicit. The recursive account would be inadequate if it allowed an operative standard to remain immune while claiming criticism had effect, or required a final evaluator for local progress. The transport account would fail if it disconnected legitimate revolutions or admitted arbitrary changes as solutions. The universality conditions would need revision if their resource clauses covertly supplied every achievement, if their domains were selected by successes, or if the understanding-creating distinction misdescribed universal ability. An attribution of \(\mathrm{UED}\) would be challenged by a genuine organizational barrier to an independently characterized domain under enabling conditions that do not remove the barrier by replacing the system.

**K-STANDING** would need revision if a defensible account of self-criticism were found in an organization that grants standing on generation or discards what it generates, or if the distinction between retention and standing could not be applied to any realization without a theory of mechanism. **The extensible class** would need withdrawal if E1 could not be stated without a mechanistic notion of a generator, if E1 turned out to be entailed by target closure after all, or if E2 and E3 added nothing to domain-relative \(\mathrm{UED}\) as already reported. (FW2.)

Renaming an inconvenient case, changing scope silently, or declaring every negative case "not a real problem" would not answer any of these.

## Named criticism routes and conjectures

(FW2, new.) A commitment that names its strongest published opponent is more contestable than one that does not.

**Cognitive closure.** The named challenge to the attribution of \(\mathrm{UED}\) to humans is the proposal that problems lacking part-whole and lawful-relation structure are constitutionally beyond a combinatorial mind. It concedes the coherence of the universal class and contests membership; in this theory's terms it asserts that humans are in \(\mathrm{EX}\setminus\mathrm{UED}\). Its obligations are stated in Part III. Its published counter-argument is that any explanation comprehensible to a universal explainer is comprehensible to a person, so closure would require that the barred problems have no explanation; that argument is itself a conjecture about reach and is eligible for criticism on the same terms. [P1; B3; B6]

**The jump conjecture.** \(\mathrm{EX}_{\Theta,\beta}=\mathrm{UED}_{\Theta,\beta}\): an organization that has extended itself into one independently specified domain by criticizing and revising its own generator constraints, traceably, has the capacity to do so for any admitted domain, the remaining differences between domains being differences in \(\chi\). This is this theory's form of the claim that universality arrives as a jump. It is refuted by an organization shown to be in \(\mathrm{EX}\) and shown, by an organizational argument meeting the closure obligations, to be barred from some domain. If it holds, the extensible class is not proper on that side and its value is to name the condition that makes the jump possible; if it fails, closure has a member. [B6]

**Two layers of error correction.** Any physical realization of the kernel contains a fidelity-correcting layer over representations and a content-correcting layer over contents, the second not obtainable by iterating the first. This is refuted by an organization with a single error-correcting layer that instantiates the kernel, or by evidence that content-level criticism co-varies strictly with representational stability so that no dissociation can be produced. The research program that tests it is external to this authority. [H1; CT1]

## What is and is not established

The theory supplies a recursive organization of semantic roles, an explicit universal target class, a stratified hierarchy between recursion and universality, and distinctions that prevent false identifications: history with judgment, criticism with rejection, understanding with transmission, explanatory progress with persistence, recursion with universality, recursion with extensibility, productivity with creativity, general learning with explanatory organization, consensus with warrant, and physical task capacity with creativity.

It does not derive the existence of an actual universal explainer from definitions. It does not give a complete reductive account of explanation, meaning, causal authorship, progress, or creative capacity. The constructions make additional commitments explicit; their success must be assessed by the explanations they support and the criticisms they survive. The remaining question is explanatory: what organization makes the attributed capacities possible, how do its parts do the claimed work, and why do the distinctions hold. The same kernel applies to attempts to answer it.

## Refinement without semantic substitution

A specification adopting this theory distinguishes a **semantic assertion**, an **attribution judgment**, a **record fact**, and a **machine-check result**. A machine may check that a document has required fields, that a finite derivation uses stated premises, that a counterfactual experiment met a stated comparison, or that a content's own stated operands satisfy a relation it asserts. None of these establishes that its interpretation of explanation, reason use, authorship, progress, or capacity is correct.

Let \(A\) be the interpretation of this authority and \(D\) a dossier or implementation state. A refinement provides a partial interpretation relation \(\mathcal I(D,A)\), not a definition of \(A\) as whatever the implementation accepts. For every projected claim it states subject, scope, interpretation, dependencies, and whether the projection concerns a record fact, a situated judgment, or semantic satisfaction. A machine-level classification may entail a semantic proposition only under an explicit bridge whose adequacy is open to criticism. A restrictive profile can require an explicit graph, an intervention family, a finite event vocabulary, or a witness format; failure to satisfy it is failure of that check, not absence of the phenomenon; passing it is not a definition. The connection must be substantive in both directions and must test legitimate cases against unintended exclusion: inherited targets, communicated reconstruction, inexplicit contributions, method change, nonreplacement results, provisional closure.

Admission, use, and truth are distinct (K-STANDING). Recording a proposed case does not make its body satisfy its checks; satisfying checks does not make premises true; a mechanically failed body must not be reported as passed because nobody objected. Noninductivism forbids manufacturing warrant from a count of endorsements or repetitions, from agreement among instances or components, from attestation, or from a count of satisfied constraints; it does not make different arguments or new information irrelevant because they share a conclusion. Operational stopping and epistemic immunity are different. A specification may itself be criticized through the inquiry it supports; a replacement can be enacted by a person, institution, or mechanism without a self-rewriting evaluator, and the account must identify the criticism, replacement, decision, and effects. Version labels establish traceability, not return relevance.

## Further discriminating cases

**Delayed reconstruction.** A relay emits a received explanation at \(e_1\) without reconstructing it; the system develops the understanding at \(e_2\). Authorship at \(e_2\) cannot combine with novelty and attempted use at \(e_1\) to establish \(\mathrm{OCA}\) at \(e_1\).

**Inherited target, original criticism.** An investigator inherits a theory, notices a defect, and creates an explanation of it. A creative critical episode is possible though the investigator did not originate the theory and the new explanation is not its descendant; a definition requiring lineage excludes this.

**Ordinary premise under criticism.** A criticism depends essentially on an observation interpretation rather than a labeled standard; withdrawing it removes that application's support without refuting the criticism's conclusion or reinstating the theory.

**Same target, different achievement.** A tutor supplies a complete explanation and the learner reconstructs it; this creates knowledge for the learner without establishing the capacity to originate it under an achievement condition excluding a supplied solution.

**One system, two boundaries.** (FW2.) A person's grammar-acquisition subsystem is in the first-layer class: it reconstructs an inherited system from positive evidence, denies standing to what it generates, and instantiates no kernel. The person, at the boundary that includes notation, explicit grammar, and communication, is a candidate for the extensible class. Attributions are made at boundaries; the same physical system can host members of different classes at different \(\beta\).

---

# Research program (external to the authority)

The program that tests the two-layer conjecture, the retention discriminator, and the realization constraints against a settling substrate and against an organization of language models under a host is stated in addendum A2 (hash above) and is not part of the semantics. Its products enter this authority only as constraints on \(\Theta\) modules in the manner of the realization section, and only after audit.

---

# Source keys and attribution boundaries

**F1 - David Deutsch, *The Fabric of Reality*.** Chapter 1, printed pages 2 to 13 and 19 to 28. Explanation versus prediction, creative subsidiary explanation, autonomous higher-level explanation.

**F3 - David Deutsch, *The Fabric of Reality*.** Chapter 3, printed pages 59 to 70, principally 67 to 68. Anti-inductivism, problem-directed conjecture and criticism, recursive subsidiary inquiry, the comparison with biological evolution.

**B1 - David Deutsch, *The Beginning of Infinity* (2011).** Chapter 1, printed pages 24 to 32. Explanatory constraint, reach, rules of thumb.

**B3 - David Deutsch, *The Beginning of Infinity*.** Chapter 3, "The Spark." People as universal explainers; explanatory reach not bounded by the explainer's origins. (FW2: added for the closure counter-argument.)

**B6 - David Deutsch, *The Beginning of Infinity*.** Chapter 6, printed pages 145 to 147. The jump to universality; existing reach versus historical use. The UU/UC/UED decomposition and the extensible class are modeling proposals, not Deutsch's formulas.

**B7 - David Deutsch, *The Beginning of Infinity*.** Chapter 7, printed pages 155 to 157. Explanatory attribution of the origin of knowledge; insufficiency of a behavior-only criterion.

**B14 - David Deutsch, *The Beginning of Infinity*.** Chapter 14, printed pages 364 to 368. Inexplicit explanatory knowledge; the objective-aesthetics proposal.

**B16 - David Deutsch, *The Beginning of Infinity*.** Chapter 16, printed pages 411 to 415. Creative reconstruction in transmission.

**M5 - Chiara Marletto, *The Science of Can and Can't* (2021).** Chapter 5. Generalized and abstract catalysts; information contributing to its own preservation.

**M7 - Chiara Marletto, *The Science of Can and Can't*.** Chapter 7. Counterfactual knowledge; creativity as knowledge creation by thinking.

**CT1 - David Deutsch and Chiara Marletto, "Constructor theory of information," *Proceedings of the Royal Society A* (2015).** Information media; copying and distinguishability; error correction as a condition of retained capacity. (FW2.)

**H1 - Jeff Hawkins, *A Thousand Brains* (2021).** Chapters 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, and 12 to 16. Used for contrast cases and as a candidate \(\Theta\) module; the extension of reference frames to conceptual knowledge is, by its author's statement, speculative. Not adopted. (FW2.)

**H2 - Hawkins, Lewis, Klukas, Purdy, Ahmad, "A Framework for Intelligence and Cortical Function Based on Grid Cells in the Neocortex," *Frontiers in Neural Circuits* 12 (2019).** Primary statement of the frames-and-columns account. (FW2.)

**H5, H6 - Clay, Leadholm, Hawkins, "The Thousand Brains Project" (2024); Leadholm et al., "Thousand-Brains Systems," *Neural Computation* (2025).** The open implementation used in the extension-by-replacement case. (FW2.)

**P1 - Steven Pinker, *How the Mind Works* (1997).** Chapter 2 for the combinatorial medium; chapter 8, final section, for cognitive closure. The evolutionary psychology and the correlational account of information are not adopted. (FW2.)

**P2 - Steven Pinker, *Learnability and Cognition*, new edition (2013; first 1989).** Chapter 1 for the logical problem and Baker's paradox; chapter 4 for possible and actual forms; chapter 7 for the unlearning problem and listedness; chapter 8 for the resolution and spatial schemas. The linguistic analyses are not adopted; the property-/existence-predicting distinction is J. D. Fodor's as the source states. (FW2.)

**Attribution boundary.** The distinctions in this document are its own. The sources marked (FW2) supplied mechanisms, positions, and worked domains against which those distinctions are exhibited; none proposes this theory or its classes, and none is committed to them.

---

# Change register: FW2 against FW1a

| Location | Change | Origin |
|---|---|---|
| Part I-A, K-PROBLEM | Frames as background; frame choice content-bearing | A1.5, C2.5 |
| Part I-A, K-CRITICISM | Three non-criticism mechanisms named | A1.2, A1.3, A3.1 |
| Part I-A, K-RECURSION | Realization-side complement (rules executed, not consulted) | C1.5 |
| Part I-A, K-STANDING | New core commitment | C2.2, A3.2 |

| Part I-A, K-PROGRESS | No direction or terminus; transport not incorporation | A1.6 |
| Part I-A, K-UNIVERSALITY | Revisable generator constraints in the capacity; learning checklist insufficient | C2.3, E1, A1.1 |

| Part II, attempting | Prediction is not explanation; statistical "explaining away" | A1, A2 |

| Part II, dependencies | Evolved constraints as provisional background | C1.3 |
| Part II, appraisal | Consensus mechanisms represent no appraisal | A1.3 |
| Part II, newness | Initial repertoire domain \(D_0\) defined | E1 |

| Part II, quality | Constraint satisfaction is not probability; two reaches | A1.4, C1.5 |
| Part II, progress | Loss does not undo creation | A1.6 |
| Part II, universality | Record is not barrier; learnability as template | C1.2, C2.1 |

| Part II, physical realization | Six realization constraints | C1.1, A2, A3, C2.2 |
| Part III | Seventeen cases added | A1, A3, C1, C2, E1 |
| Part IV, count against | K-STANDING and EX refutation conditions | C2, E1 |
| Part IV, named routes | Closure; jump conjecture; two layers | C1.2, E1, A2 |
| Part IV, refinement | Noninductivism extended to agreement, attestation, constraint counts | A1.3, A1.4, A3.1 |
| Part IV, further cases | One system, two boundaries | E1 |
| Source keys | B3, CT1, H1, H2, H5, H6, P1, P2 added | all |

Nothing in FW1a is withdrawn. Every formal definition of FW1a appears unchanged. An audit should confirm this by checking each display against FW1a, confirm that each row of the register cites an addendum whose derivation the audit has separately accepted, and confirm that K-STANDING and \(\mathrm{EX}\) satisfy the refutation conditions stated in Part IV rather than being defined so as to be unrefutable.

1	# FW5 JUMP from FW2+FW3+FW4 - Explanatory construction
2	
3	## Where this belongs
4	
5	**Role:** new structural framework proposal. **Predecessors and inputs:** [FW2](../FW2%20JUMP%20from%20FW1a%20-%20Standing%20and%20capacity%20classes/FW2%20JUMP%20from%20FW1a%20-%20Standing%20and%20capacity%20hierarchy.md), [D1](../FW2%20JUMP%20from%20FW1a%20-%20Standing%20and%20capacity%20classes/D1%20FROM%20FW2%20-%20What%20knowledge%20cannot%20be.md), [D2](../FW2%20JUMP%20from%20FW1a%20-%20Standing%20and%20capacity%20classes/D2%20FROM%20FW2%2BD1%20-%20When%20accounts%20cannot%20hold.md), [D3](../FW2%20JUMP%20from%20FW1a%20-%20Standing%20and%20capacity%20classes/D3%20FROM%20FW2%2BD1%2BD2%20-%20What%20work%20cannot%20be.pdf), [FW3](../FW3%20AMEND%20of%20FW2%20-%20Introducing%20why-dependence/FW3%20AMEND%20of%20FW2%20via%20D1-D3%20-%20Why-dependence.md), [FW4](../FW4%20RELATED%20to%20FW3%20-%20Structural%20discharge/FW4%20RELATED%20to%20FW3%20-%20Structural%20discharge.md), [M4](../00%20ORIGINS%20-%20Sources%20and%20missing%20links/M4%20MISSING%20-%20Four%20exact%20inputs%20to%20FW5.md), [O1](../00%20ORIGINS%20-%20Sources%20and%20missing%20links/O1%20SOURCE-CITED%20-%20Deutsch%20books.md), [O2](../00%20ORIGINS%20-%20Sources%20and%20missing%20links/O2%20SOURCE-CITED%20-%20Constructor%20theory.md).
6	
7	Replaces the residual Because primitive in the core definition with a structural account subject to anchoring, fidelity, question fidelity, non-circular dependence, and non-vacuity. Integrates critical inquiry, provenance, retained physical capabilities, and the universal-capacity question.
8	
9	A new proposal, not a silently conservative amendment. Its adequacy claim remains conjectural. Historical source name: ECS 1.0, not V3.
10	
11	**Where it leads:** [Q3](01%20AUDIT%20-%20Criticisms%20of%20FW5/Q3%20AUDIT%20of%20FW5%20-%20Structural%20weaknesses.md), [Q4](01%20AUDIT%20-%20Criticisms%20of%20FW5/Q4%20AUDIT%20of%20FW5%20-%20Proofs%20and%20anti-smuggling.md), [D4](02%20FROM%20-%20The%20audit%20theory/D4%20FROM%20FW5%20-%20Audits%20and%20conformance.md), [T3](04%20TEST%20-%20Language-model%20study/T3%20TEST%20of%20FW5%20-%20Language-model%20study.md).
12	
13	**Basis for this placement:** Opening standing and constitutive conjecture; structural-answer definition; predecessor discussion; exact original S1-S6 source hashes.
14	
15	[Naming key and family tree](../layout.md). The navigation above is editorial. The manuscript below is a renamed reading edition, not a new scientific revision. Original hashes, case identifiers, mathematical symbols, quoted locators, and execution commands retain their historical meaning. Hashes bind the unchanged originals, not this reading copy.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## A structural, recursive semantic class of creativity
20	
21	**Archive name:** FW5. **Date:** 8 September 2026. **Standing:** a new proposal, not an assertion of adoption and not an amendment that silently preserves every claim of its predecessors.
22	
23	## The proposal in ordinary language
24	
25	A creative thinker does not merely produce an unusual answer. It constructs or reconstructs an organization of ideas through which a difficulty can be understood, investigated, or transformed. That organization can be mistaken. When it actually removes an explanatory defect, the achievement is knowledge creation in the relevant respect. When the thinker can turn the same activity on its own interpretations, methods, and restrictions, with consequences for how it proceeds, the organization is recursively critical. When no subject-specific barrier permanently confines that capacity, the stronger attribution is explanatory universality.
26	
27	The central proposal of this document is that an explanation represents a **question-relevant organization of dependencies**, not merely a set of true sentences or a successful input–output mapping. What makes a dependency explanatory is not a label attached to it. The explanation must preserve the target's relevant organization under the distinctions and changes the question concerns. Producing an effect, identifying an unknown quantity, deriving an obstruction, constituting a status, and making an artistic feature serve a purpose are different questions. A representation that silently substitutes one for another is inadequate even when its arithmetic is correct.
28	
29	Creativity concerns the construction and use of such representations. Constructor theory constrains their physical realization and the capabilities their instantiation makes available. Creating knowledge can change an organization's accessible capabilities or its use of existing ones; it does not change the laws of physics or convert a physically impossible task into a possible one.
30	
31	The mathematics used here is ordinary set theory, relational structures, counterfactual interventions, and modal transition semantics. Neither computability nor uncomputability is a membership condition. There is no objective function, ranking of thinkers or conjectures, probability of truth, mandatory formal submission, or final judge.
32	
33	**Constitutive conjecture.** Explanatory creativity can be characterized by the construction of question-relevant dependency representations, their content-sensitive use and criticism, and their physically grounded provenance. The definitions below make that conjecture precise. The conjecture is not a theorem about every possible mind. A genuine explanatory achievement that cannot satisfy the structural conditions would count against it.
34	
35	## What “no gaps” can responsibly mean
36	
37	Every defined predicate in this class has a stated interpretation and terminates in declared mathematical data. There is no residual primitive named `Because`, `ExplanatoryWork`, `GoodExplanation`, or `Creative`. The central explanatory predicate is defined through structural conditions rather than through a synonym for explanation.
38	
39	That does not remove the need for substantive theories of the world. A physical law, the meaning of an expression, and a normative reason are not derived from a transcript by set theory. Their interpretations are declared inputs to a model, and applications of the model are conjectures. The distinction is essential: a complete mathematical definition of a model class is not complete knowledge of which model describes reality.
40	
41	In particular, objective aesthetics cannot honestly be obtained by defining beauty as approval, symmetry, compression, surprise, or successful persuasion. This class gives normative and artistic questions an explicit semantic place without pretending to have discovered all their true substantive premises. It makes that dependence visible rather than leaving an undefined aesthetic module or claiming that a new notation has solved aesthetics.
42	
43	# The commitments
44	
45	## Explanatory realism and fallibility
46	
47	Whether a representation preserves a target's relevant organization is independent of whether anyone accepts it. A system can be wrong about its interpretation, its observations, its criticism, its progress, or its own capacities. A mathematically valid derivation can be applied to the wrong target. Conversely, a correct explanation can remain unrecognized.
48	
49	Knowledge need not be an entirely true theory. A theory can contain an accurate account of a scoped dependence together with erroneous claims elsewhere. An approximation can correctly describe an explicitly approximate feature. What cannot count as successful explanation is an error in the very dependence alleged to account for that feature. This separates partial truth from truth-certification, and fallibility from the claim that falsehood itself performs explanatory work.
50	
51	Deutsch's account of knowledge as conjectured explanations, typically containing both truth and error, motivates this treatment. The present formal definitions are not his formulas. [R1]
52	
53	## Conjecture, criticism, and action
54	
55	An idea may be entertained without first being justified. Its generation neither proves it nor obliges a thinker to use it. Conjecture precedes criticism in the sense that a criticism has a target; that target can be an inherited or inexplicit expectation. A criticism is itself conjectural.
56	
57	A thinker may act on an appraisal without having certified it. Withholding a premise, retaining a theory, revising a question, or moving on are possible actions. They are not truth-conferring events. Refusing an infallible evaluator must not be turned into a requirement that no criticism can ever affect practice.
58	
59	Observation, deduction, computation, selection, feedback, communication, and biological inheritance may participate in creativity. None is sufficient merely by occurring. The invalid inference from “not sufficient” to “cannot participate” is explicitly excluded.
60	
61	## Recursive scrutiny without prior authorization
62	
63	A problem, value, standard, observation model, interpretation, inferential practice, attention policy, attribution boundary, or conjecture-generating restriction can itself become a problem. A result of that inquiry must be able to affect the operative target. Scrutiny that can never change anything is not the recursive capacity described here.
64	
65	No inquiry must first complete a proof of the legitimacy of all its methods. Present methods can be used provisionally while particular difficulties in them are examined. A system can represent a method without rewriting the physical laws that implement it.
66	
67	## Substrate independence with physical obligations
68	
69	A sentence, diagram, internal model, imagined movement, artistic discrimination, or distributed practice may carry relevant organization. No complete translation into a formal language is required of the thinker. The mathematical representation is an account of the relevant organization, not an admission form that every thought must complete.
70	
71	Physical realization is nevertheless substantive. The claimed distinctions, transformations, and retained capacities must be permitted by the adopted physical theory. Abstract consistency alone is not evidence of physical realizability.
72	
73	# Mathematical foundations
74	
75	## Ambient mathematics and size
76	
77	Work in classical set theory. Every individual model has set-sized domains. A class of models may be proper. The domains, relations, histories, and sets of commitments may be infinite. No enumeration, finite axiomatization, compactness property, minimal support, or decision procedure is assumed unless a result explicitly states one.
78	
79	Classical truth in the metatheory does not require classical deductive closure in the thinker. A model may describe a person entertaining mutually inconsistent claims without asserting those claims as truths. The system's appraisals and the model's satisfaction relation are different objects.
80	
81	## Organizations
82	
83	An organization is a structure
84	
85	\[
86	D=(V,(X_v)_{v\in V},J,B,A,L,\operatorname{role}).
87	\]
88	
89	Here \(V\) is a set of ports or variables, and each \(X_v\) is its nonempty value domain. A valuation is an element of \(X_D=\prod_{v\in V}X_v\). The set \(J\) indexes components. A component may be a physical assignment, a measurement relation, a mathematical constraint, a constitutive rule, or another explicitly interpreted relation. Its footprint \(V_j\subseteq V\) specifies the ports it connects.
90	
91	The set \(B\) contains boundary conditions. The set \(A\) contains admitted edits and their composable sequences, including an identity edit \(1\). Composition is associative wherever defined, with stated typing conditions. Edits may change inputs, replace a component, delete an assumption, alter an observation interpretation, or change a rule. Not every conceivable edit must be physically possible.
92	
93	For each \(j\in J\), edit \(a\in A\), and boundary condition \(b\in B\), the interpretation supplies a relation
94	
95	\[
96	L_j(a,b)\subseteq\prod_{v\in V_j}X_v.
97	\]
98	
99	The compatible valuations are exactly
100	
101	\[
102	\operatorname{Sol}_D(a,b)
103	=
104	\{z\in X_D:\forall j\in J,
105	\ z|_{V_j}\in L_j(a,b)\}.
106	\tag{O}
107	\]
108	
109	Deleted components impose the full relation on their ports. A causal intervention that sets a variable replaces its assignment; it does not merely add an observational equation while retaining an incompatible assignment. A change of a rule is a change of a component, not evidence that the original rule had already changed.
110	
111	The role interpretation fixes which ports are independent inputs, produced outputs, observations, control states, rule applications, and so forth. It also fixes what component edits mean. These distinctions are part of the substantive target model, not supplied by the direction in which someone happens to solve an equation.
112	
113	Entire paths, functions, fields, proof structures, or histories may be values of ports. Equation (O) therefore does not restrict a domain to finite graphs, instantaneous states, linear systems, or acyclic dependence. Cyclic equilibrium constraints are admitted without treating them as backward historical causation. When a model has several solutions, they remain several solutions; a preferred one is not silently selected.
114	
115	## Questions and their contracts
116	
117	A question is an indexed structure
118	
119	\[
120	p=(D,\Sigma,b_0,\kappa,\mathcal C,\mathcal Q,O_p).
121	\]
122	
123	The target is \(D\). The scope \(\Sigma\subseteq A\times B\) fixes which edits and boundary conditions are in the claim. The distinguished baseline is \((1,b_0)\in\Sigma\). The respect \(\kappa\) fixes what is asked: for example, production, inferential identification, impossibility, rule-governed status, achievement of an aim, or aesthetic value. The contrast contract \(\mathcal C\subseteq A\times B\), with its associated role and edit specifications, fixes the input changes, component changes, and distinctions material to that question. It includes the baseline and is not identified with a collection of performed experiments.
124	
125	The query operator \(\mathcal Q\) is a specified set-theoretic operation on the relevant organization, its solutions, and, where needed, its component structure. Its codomain \(Y_p\) is specified. It may return a feature value, a set of compatible values, a reachability relation, the truth value of an obstruction, a derivation property, or a normative application. The answer profile is
126	
127	\[
128	\operatorname{Ans}_p(a,b)
129	=
130	\mathcal Q(D,a,b).
131	\tag{Q}
132	\]
133	
134	The set \(O_p\) contains the obligations being addressed or protected by an inquiry about \(p\). Each obligation is a specified condition on a resulting situation, not an automatically optimized objective.
135	
136	The contract states which quantities may be supplied as independent boundary facts and which quantity or dependence is to be accounted for. A question about what produces an output cannot be answered by installing that output as an unexplained input and relabelling an inverse calculation as a production process.
137	
138	A question can be posed mistakenly. The occurrence of its formulation is still a real event. It may fail to pick out the alleged target, assume an impossible baseline, confuse two respects, or combine incompatible requirements. Exposing that defect is another question with its own target and contract. “Why did the nonexistent event happen?” and “Why does this question presuppose an event that did not happen?” are not the same question.
139	
140	The question contract is not immune. It can be criticized and replaced. What is prohibited is changing it during an assessment without recording the resulting change in what is claimed.
141	
142	## Contents and occurrences
143	
144	An occurrence is a particular physically or historically located carrier. A content is an interpreted organization, including its commitments, connections, reference, and scope. Occurrences are not identified merely because they carry the same words. Contents are not identified merely because they have the same truth value or final output.
145	
146	An interpretation at grain \(\ell\) may assign a content to a token, a disposition, or an organized collection of occurrences. The representation relation
147	
148	\[
149	\operatorname{Rep}_{\beta,\ell}(o,c,h)
150	\]
151	
152	is declared model data about reference and representation at boundary \(\beta\). It is not a host's claim that the token was supplied to a prompt. Its admissibility requires preservation of the relevant bindings and transformations in the realization conditions below.
153	
154	A grain fixes which structural distinctions count as differences for the attribution at issue. A genuine recoding is an isomorphism of the retained structure at that grain. Coarsening is not automatically an isomorphism. Bundling two commitments into one can change the answer to a question about individual contribution while preserving an answer about their joint organization.
155	
156	The representation relation is an explicit semantic primitive. Removing the word “explanation” from a formula does not derive reference from uninterpreted matter. Here reference has a different job from explanatory adequacy: a system can represent a false explanation, misidentify a target, or understand a criticism that is wrong. Those possibilities would be lost if representation itself meant successful explanation.
157	
158	# Explanatory adequacy without a `Because` primitive
159	
160	## A structural answer
161	
162	An explanatory candidate for \(p\) supplies an organization \(E\), an answer profile \(\operatorname{Ans}_E\), and an interpretation of its active commitments. The commitments actually claimed to account for the target must be distinguished from incidental remarks. This distinction is part of the interpreted claim, not permission for an assessor to rescue a failed argument by selecting whichever fragments happen to be true.
163	
164	A structural account consists of
165	
166	\[
167	\mathcal E=(E,p,\pi,\tau,\sigma,\lambda).
168	\]
169	
170	The map \(\pi\) sends target valuations in the stated scope to explanatory valuations. It may be many-to-one. The maps \(\tau\) and \(\sigma\) translate edits and boundary conditions. The map \(\lambda\) anchors explanatory components to target components or specified subnetworks. All maps have declared domains. Their meanings are held fixed across the comparison.
171	
172	The following conditions define \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\).
173	
174	**Anchoring.** Every active explanatory component has a stated target interpretation under \(\lambda\). Its port roles and edit semantics are preserved. A causal assignment must be anchored to a causal assignment or a derived causal suborganization, not merely to an observed association. A measurement relation must be anchored to a measurement organization. A constitutive rule must be anchored to the rule it purports to apply. A derived suborganization is evaluated using (O), including its hidden ports and boundary conditions; the word “derived” does not authorize an unexplained explanatory arrow.
175	
176	More formally, the anchoring data include a port translation for each component, depending only on the ports of its anchored subnetwork and the explicitly declared boundary. The target subnetwork's relation is obtained by imposing its component constraints and projecting away its hidden ports. That projected relation must equal the explanatory component relation at the declared abstraction. Port-role translations must agree, and every component edit in the contrast contract must translate to the corresponding replacement of that subnetwork relation. Together with (F), which checks the assembled organization, this prevents local relation matches from silently losing constraints shared between components. These are equalities and typing conditions on supplied relations, not an additional unexplained relevance predicate.
177	
178	
179	**Structural fidelity.** For the comparisons specified in \(\Sigma\cap\mathcal C\),
180	
181	\[
182	\pi[\operatorname{Sol}_D(a,b)]
183	=
184	\operatorname{Sol}_E(\tau(a),\sigma(b)).
185	\tag{F}
186	\]
187	
188	The translation preserves identities and every composition for which a claim is made:
189	
190	\[
191	\tau(1)=1,
192	\qquad
193	\tau(a_2a_1)=\tau(a_2)\tau(a_1).
194	\tag{C}
195	\]
196	
197	Component surgeries must commute with their anchors. Replacing an explanatory component cannot be interpreted as changing an unrelated part of the target solely to obtain the desired answer. Equations (F) and (C) are applied at the stated abstraction and scope, not to every microscopic feature of the world.
198	
199	**Question fidelity.** For the same comparisons,
200	
201	\[
202	\operatorname{Ans}_E(\tau(a),\sigma(b))
203	=
204	\operatorname{Ans}_p(a,b).
205	\tag{A}
206	\]
207	
208	This includes the respect \(\kappa\), not just a matching number. The contract ranges over the declared class of changes, including unperformed changes, not merely over the trials on which the candidate succeeded. An account of identifiability must answer an identifiability question. An account of an audience's response does not, by that fact, answer a question about objective aesthetic merit.
209	
210	**Non-circular dependence.** The answer follows by evaluating the anchored organization under its declared independent boundary conditions. The target answer is not an unanalysed boundary input or a copied target assertion among its premises. Moving the same target assertion from an input slot into a component called a law does not remove this prohibition. Identity of that assertion is structural at the declared grain, not the indiscriminate identification of all logically equivalent mathematical truths. There is at least one admitted contrast that removes or changes a nonempty block of active organizational commitments, while preserving the other declared boundary conditions, for which the answer profile changes or ceases to be determined in the claimed way. The contrast may concern a counterfactual law or rule rather than a physically executable intervention. Its formal meaning must still be stated.
211	
212	**Non-vacuity.** The baseline organization has a compatible state or history. A claim of impossibility may correctly assert that a specified goal has no compatible realization, but not infer a substantive result merely from an inconsistent baseline. A contrast family containing only notational variants, or one defined to exclude every change that could matter, does not meet non-circular dependence.
213	
214	Thus
215	
216	\[
217	\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)
218	\iff
219	\operatorname{Anchor}\land\operatorname{Fidelity}
220	\land\operatorname{QuestionFidelity}
221	\land\operatorname{NonCircularDependence}
222	\land\operatorname{NonVacuity}.
223	\tag{E}
224	\]
225	
226	The right side is determined by the specified structures and maps. It contains no predicate that already means “really explains.” Anchoring is a claim about the kind and organization of the target's components; fidelity is a collection of mathematical equalities; question fidelity is an indexing condition; non-circular dependence is a contrast property.
227	
228	This is a substantive proposal about explanation, not a logical consequence of realism alone. Its strongest claim is that these structural requirements, correctly interpreted, capture explanatory accounting. If a genuine explanation requires a distinction no such structure can preserve, the proposal must change. An unsupported exemption saying that the example nevertheless satisfies a primitive `Because` is not available.
229	
230	## What the definition excludes—and what it does not
231	
232	A table of observed answers need not have an anchoring to the target's causal, constitutive, or inferential organization. Matching the table therefore does not establish (E). A table that really encodes an entire relevant organization under its interventions is a different case: the representation's tabular notation is not a reason to exclude it. Anti-behaviorism is a distinction about organization, not a ban on a data structure.
233	
234	“\(p\), because \(p\)” fails when the conclusion is simply installed as the independent premise and no separate organizational constraint explains it. A true mechanism guessed for bad reasons can nevertheless meet (E); the guesser's grounds can be defective without making the mechanism false. Circular support for accepting a mechanism must therefore be distinguished from a circular explanatory structure.
235	
236	Explanatory depth is question-relative. A derivation may answer “why does this follow under these rules?” while failing to answer “what caused this event?” A proof can be adequate to a specified mathematical question without being the deepest or most illuminating account available. Equation (E) is not a universal measure of elegance or merit.
237	
238	Nor is all explanation globally asymmetric. Production can be directed; equilibrium constraints can mutually determine quantities; different respects can support different directions. What must be preserved is the particular dependency organization, not an untyped axiom that every explanatory relation has the same directionality.
239	
240	## Why the structural bridge is not a certificate
241	
242	A mathematician can establish that (F) holds for two described structures without establishing that either describes the intended physical target. A thinker can propose an anchor that is wrong. A question contract can omit a distinction the original difficulty requires. These are different criticism targets.
243	
244	No separate approval event creates an account. The maps can exist before anyone discovers them. An investigator's successful argument for their existence is evidence for the attribution, not its truth-maker by decree. A thinker need not possess the maps in explicit notation to instantiate the relevant organization.
245	
246	The previous separation into a mathematical claim, an application claim, and a relevance claim was pointing in the right direction. The further commitment here is explicit: a complete account also preserves **component-level organization under the appropriate kinds of change**. There is no assertion that any mathematical theorem plus any independently testable application claim automatically constitutes an explanation.
247	
248	# Work, redundancy, interference, and infinity
249	
250	## Support families without a minimality assumption
251	
252	Fix an interpreted candidate, a question, its background, and a declared restriction operation. For \(W\subseteq\Gamma\), let \(E|W\) be the organization obtained by retaining the commitments in \(W\) in the specified roles while keeping the named background fixed. Removing a commitment does not assert its negation. Removing a sentence from an archive does not automatically perform this semantic restriction.
253	
254	Define
255	
256	\[
257	\mathsf S_{E,p}
258	=
259	\{W\subseteq\Gamma:
260	\operatorname{Account}(E|W,p)
261	\}.
262	\tag{S}
263	\]
264	
265	The suppressed maps in this notation are the restricted, declared maps of the original interpretation. A new map or a changed role assignment is a different route, which must be identified as such.
266	
267	No upward closure is assumed. Adding an active, incompatible premise can spoil a route. No minimal member is assumed. The whole family, rather than a selected minimal subset, is the basic support object.
268	
269	## Individual and collective contribution
270	
271	For \(W\subseteq\Gamma\) and a nonempty block \(D\subseteq W\), define
272	
273	\[
274	\operatorname{CriticalBlock}(D;W,p)
275	\iff
276	W\in\mathsf S_{E,p}
277	\land W\setminus D\notin\mathsf S_{E,p}.
278	\tag{B}
279	\]
280	
281	An individual commitment is contributory in this deletion respect when it is a critical block of size one in some support. A block may contribute without any singleton in it doing so. The absence of a singleton witness must not be called absence of explanatory organization.
282	
283	Replacement contrasts need not be deletion contrasts. For a declared family \(\mathcal V\) of organization edits, define
284	
285	\[
286	\operatorname{Boundary}_{E,p}
287	=
288	\{(v,w)\in\mathcal V^2:
289	\operatorname{Account}(E_v,p)
290	\ne\operatorname{Account}(E_w,p)\}.
291	\tag{D}
292	\]
293	
294	Each pair retains its edited components, background, and interpretation. The boundary records where an account survives or fails; it does not assign a probability or a score. Positive contribution, interference, substitution, and jointly necessary organization can all be represented in this unrestricted family.
295	
296	## The finite monotone theorem
297	
298	Suppose \(\Gamma\) is finite, \(\mathsf S\subseteq\mathcal P(\Gamma)\) is upward closed, and \(\Gamma\in\mathsf S\). Let \(\min\mathsf S\) be its inclusion-minimal members. Then
299	
300	\[
301	\{d:\exists W\in\mathsf S,
302	\ d\in W,
303	\ W\setminus\{d\}\notin\mathsf S\}
304	=
305	\bigcup\min\mathsf S,
306	\tag{M1}
307	\]
308	
309	and
310	
311	\[
312	\{d:\Gamma\setminus\{d\}\notin\mathsf S\}
313	=
314	\bigcap\min\mathsf S.
315	\tag{M2}
316	\]
317	
318	**Proof.** A member of a minimal support is critical for that support. Conversely, if \(d\) is critical for \(W\), finiteness supplies a minimal support \(U\subseteq W\). If \(d\notin U\), upward closure would make \(W\setminus\{d\}\) a support, a contradiction. For (M2), deletion of \(d\) preserves support exactly when a minimal support omitting \(d\) exists. The original support assumption prevents the intersection statement from relying on an empty family. ∎
319	
320	The theorem is a conditional result about supports, not a theorem that every explanation has a minimal proof or every working detail is indispensable.
321	
322	## Redundant routes
323	
324	Let \(\Gamma=\{a,b\}\) and
325	
326	\[
327	\mathsf S=\{\{a\},\{b\},\{a,b\}\}.
328	\]
329	
330	Both commitments have an individual contribution witness. Neither is indispensable to the full organization. Removing both defeats every route. Redundancy can make a realization resilient; it does not make each route meaningless or automatically make the explanation bad.
331	
332	Two systems with the same output table can have different active routes. In parallel wiring, both routes may be active. In priority wiring, the first may prevent the second from firing. A token-level authorship or causal attribution requires the internal event structure. Endpoint agreement establishes neither identity of active causes nor identity of contributors.
333	
334	## Interference
335	
336	Let success at a fixed scope require \(a\) and the absence of an interfering active commitment \(b\). Then
337	
338	\[
339	\mathsf S=\{\{a\}\}
340	\quad\text{on}\quad
341	\Gamma=\{a,b\}.
342	\]
343	
344	The full active candidate fails even though a restricted candidate succeeds. It is wrong to infer success of the full candidate from existence of a successful subset. It is also wrong to repair the mathematics by silently declaring \(b\) “not really a commitment.” Its interference is part of the modeled problem.
345	
346	Equations (S), (B), and (D) already handle this case. The monotone theorem simply does not apply. This is a complete semantics for the non-monotone case, not a promise that minimal-support reasoning will eventually be generalized to it.
347	
348	## Infinitary organization
349	
350	Take \(\Gamma=\{d_n:n\ge1\}\), where \(d_n\) asserts \(|x|\le1/n\). A subset of these bounds determines \(x=0\) exactly when its indices are unbounded. Every unbounded set remains unbounded after removal of one index. Hence there is a support but no minimal support and no singleton deletion witness.
351	
352	The universal family here is a stated mathematical premise, not a conclusion inferred from finitely many observed bounds. The whole family still does work. Removing an unbounded block that leaves only bounded indices destroys the determination. Equation (B) records that collective contribution without inventing a minimal block. At a coarser grain, the single content “for every \(n\ge1\), \(|x|\le1/n\)” can be individually critical. The change is in the attribution grain, not in the mathematical implication.
353	
354	**Proof of the determination.** Zero satisfies every bound. If \(|x|>0\), an unbounded index set contains \(n>1/|x|\), and the corresponding bound fails. A bounded subset has a largest relevant bound index, or is empty; it leaves a nonzero interval of compatible values. ∎
355	
356	## Hard-to-vary and reach
357	
358	Fix an organization, interpretation, variation family \(\mathcal V\), and a family \(F\) of explanatory jobs. Let
359	
360	\[
361	\operatorname{Pres}(F)
362	=
363	\{v\in\mathcal V:
364	\forall f\in F,
365	\operatorname{Account}(E_v,f)\}.
366	\]
367	
368	Then
369	
370	\[
371	F\subseteq F'
372	\ \Longrightarrow\
373	\operatorname{Pres}(F')\subseteq\operatorname{Pres}(F).
374	\tag{H}
375	\]
376	
377	**Proof.** Preserving every job in the larger family includes preserving every job in the smaller family. ∎
378	
379	That is the valid structural connection between additional reach and restrictions on variation. The containment need not be strict. It says nothing by itself about two different theories using different interpretations or different variation families. Counting jobs is not a replacement for the missing comparison.
380	
381	“Hard to vary” is therefore an articulated pattern of constrained changes, relative to an explanatory job. It is not the requirement that every detail of a complete theory be individually indispensable. Nor is it a numerical warrant. Two descriptions can divide the same work into different numbers of features; splitting one feature into ten cannot create knowledge.
382	
383	Reach occurs when an unchanged organizational core participates in an account of another question through a stated anchor and additional background. The new bridge is itself content and can be a creative contribution. No insistence that exactly the same minimal support survive is imposed.
384	
385	# Exact domain constructions
386	
387	## Production and the direction of an explanation
388	
389	Consider the stipulated structural organization
390	
391	\[
392	H:=U_H,
393	\qquad \theta:=U_\theta,
394	\qquad L:=H\cot\theta,
395	\qquad 0<\theta<\pi/2.
396	\]
397	
398	The role assignments designate \(H\) and \(\theta\) as upstream in the production of \(L\). Intervening on \(L\) replaces its last equation and does not replace the equations for \(H\) or \(\theta\). Changing \(H\) while holding \(\theta\) fixed changes \(L\). The forward account preserves the production structure. Solving the last equation for \(H\) does not reverse that structure.
399	
400	A calculation from shadow length to height can nevertheless be a correct account of **identification**. It fails only when presented as an answer to the different question of what produced the height. A pole intentionally constructed to cast a specified shadow would have a different causal organization. The direction is not settled by the nouns “pole” and “shadow.”
401	
402	This use of structural equations is informed by causal-model work, but FW5 does not import a particular published definition of actual cause as a universal definition of explanation. Actual token causes, type-level dependences, inference, and explanation remain distinct. [R6]
403	
404	## Nonlinear and constrained identification
405	
406	Let \(Z\ne\varnothing\) be the set of states admitted by the background constraints. Let \(g:Z\to Y\) be a measurement map and \(f:Z\to F\) the feature at issue. Neither map need be linear, continuous, differentiable, computable, or finite-dimensional.
407	
408	For an observed value \(y\), define its compatibility fibre
409	
410	\[
411	Z_y=\{z\in Z:g(z)=y\}.
412	\]
413	
414	The feature is identified at \(y\) exactly when
415	
416	\[
417	Z_y\ne\varnothing
418	\quad\land\quad
419	|f[Z_y]|=1.
420	\tag{I1}
421	\]
422	
423	An empty fibre is incompatibility of the stipulated observation with the model. It is not perfect identification by vacuous universal quantification.
424	
425	**Factorization theorem.** The feature is identified on every attainable measurement exactly when a function \(\bar f:g[Z]\to F\) exists such that
426	
427	\[
428	f=\bar f\circ g.
429	\tag{I2}
430	\]
431	
432	**Proof.** If \(f\) is constant on each fibre, define \(\bar f(y)\) to be that fibre's unique feature value. The definition is unambiguous and requires no choice among competing values. Conversely, if (I2) holds, equal measurement values have equal feature values. ∎
433	
434	This theorem supplies the nonlinear and constrained case directly. For example, \(g(x)=x^2\) on \(Z=\mathbb R\) does not identify the sign of a nonzero \(x\). On \(Z=[0,\infty)\), it identifies \(x\). The change is an additional domain constraint, not an improvement created by repeating the same observation. Local derivative information alone does not establish the global fibre property.
435	
436	For a measurement **relation** \(G\subseteq Z\times Y\), define \(Z_y=\{z:(z,y)\in G\}\). Equation (I1) remains the exact criterion. There is a function assigning each attainable \(y\) a unique feature value exactly when every such fibre has a singleton image. This is the relational generalization; it does not assume a hidden deterministic measurement function.
437	
438	For approximation in a specified pseudometric \(d_F\), the complete answer can remain the uncertainty set \(f[Z_y]\). A claim that all compatible values differ by at most \(\varepsilon\) means
439	
440	\[
441	\forall z,z'\in Z_y,
442	\quad d_F(f(z),f(z'))\le\varepsilon,
443	\qquad Z_y\ne\varnothing.
444	\tag{I3}
445	\]
446	
447	Equation (I3) does not automatically supply a preferred centre or an estimate with half that error. Those claims need their own premises about the space and the estimator.
448	
449	## The two balances
450	
451	The stipulated measurement model is
452	
453	\[
454	\begin{pmatrix}m_A\\m_B\end{pmatrix}
455	=
456	\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{pmatrix}
457	\begin{pmatrix}x\\b_A\\b_B\end{pmatrix}
458	=
459	\begin{pmatrix}10\\12\end{pmatrix}.
460	\]
461	
462	Its kernel is spanned by \((1,-1,-1)\). Moving along that direction changes \(x\) but leaves both readings fixed. It preserves \(b_B-b_A\). Thus the readings identify
463	
464	\[
465	b_B-b_A=2,
466	\]
467	
468	but not \(x\). This is an account of a limitation, not a failure to produce a preferred number.
469	
470	For a linear measurement map \(A\) on a real vector space and a linear feature \(c^Tz\), fibre constancy is equivalent to
471	
472	\[
473	\ker A\subseteq\ker c^T.
474	\tag{I4}
475	\]
476	
477	**Proof.** Points in one nonempty fibre differ by a kernel vector. The feature is constant on that fibre exactly when it vanishes on every such difference. ∎
478	
479	In finite dimensions, (I4) is equivalent to \(c^T\) lying in the row space of \(A\). Repetition of the same rows does not change the kernel. An independently applicable calibration can add a constraint that does.
480	
481	“Set \(b_B=0\) because that gives the mass I favor” is not an inference from the readings. The proposition \(b_B=0\) might happen to be true, in which case the augmented model can identify the mass. Its alleged evidential support is still circular. The criticism removes that route for trusting the calibration, not the logical possibility that the calibration is correct.
482	
483	This distinction repairs a recurring confusion between whether a content is correct and whether a particular argument for adopting it succeeds.
484	
485	## Invariants and obstruction
486	
487	Let \(Z\) be a state space, \(R\subseteq Z\times Z\) the allowed-step relation, and \(I:Z\to K\) a function satisfying
488	
489	\[
490	zRz'\ \Longrightarrow\ I(z)=I(z').
491	\]
492	
493	Let \(R^*\) be its finite reflexive-transitive closure. Then
494	
495	\[
496	zR^*z'\ \Longrightarrow\ I(z)=I(z').
497	\tag{O1}
498	\]
499	
500	**Proof.** Induction on the finite path length; the zero-length case is equality, and each additional step preserves \(I\). ∎
501	
502	If every goal state has an invariant value different from the initial state's value, no allowed path reaches the goal. This is a sufficient obstruction criterion, not a claim that every invariant partitions the state space into exactly the reachable components. Equal invariant values alone do not establish reachability.
503	
504	For twenty-three indivisible tokens, an equal division among three recipients would require an integer \(k\) with \(3k=23\). The obstruction is a property of the allowed integer configurations. Permitting division of tokens changes the state space and the operation contract. It does not refute the original scoped result.
505	
506	## Constitutive rules
507	
508	A constitutive system supplies states \(Z\), a rule relation \(C\subseteq Z\times S\), and a rule-identity and scope condition. The query “which status does this state have under this rule?” is answered by the fibre \(C[z]\). Existence, uniqueness, ambiguity, and inapplicability are separate cases.
509	
510	A game rule can make a configuration a win. It does not follow that the move was wise, beautiful, intended, or morally justified. Those are different queries. A correct application of an unjust rule can be criticized through a normative question about the rule itself without denying which rule was applied.
511	
512	A derivation from a rule is mathematically assessable. Whether that rule governs the practice is an application claim. Whether it should govern the practice is another claim. No vote, implementation status, or written label collapses the three.
513	
514	# Transport and preservation
515	
516	## Exact functional transport
517	
518	Suppose a target process \(S_a\) and a represented process \(T_a\) satisfy
519	
520	\[
521	\pi\circ S_a=T_a\circ\pi
522	\]
523	
524	for every admitted generator \(a\). Then the same equality holds for every admitted finite composition, provided the intermediate scopes match.
525	
526	**Proof.** For two steps,
527	
528	\[
529	\pi S_bS_a=T_b\pi S_a=T_bT_a\pi.
530	\]
531	
532	Induction gives the finite case. ∎
533	
534	The proof is about a fixed map and compatible scopes. It does not establish that two different theories share an interpretation merely because their outputs sometimes agree.
535	
536	## Relational transport
537	
538	Functional projection is not mandatory. Let \(R\subseteq Z_D\times Z_E\) relate target and explanatory valuations. A relational structural account replaces the image equality in (F) by total coverage of the relevant target solutions, coverage of the relevant explanatory solutions, and preservation of the query value for every related pair. For every admitted transition, related initial states must have matching successors under the translated label; a reverse matching condition is required for any claim of exact equivalence rather than one-sided abstraction.
539	
540	Concretely, forward preservation is
541	
542	\[
543	zRy\land z\xrightarrow{a}z'
544	\ \Longrightarrow\
545	\exists y'\,[y\xrightarrow{\tau(a)}y'\land z'Ry'].
546	\tag{T1}
547	\]
548	
549	The backward condition reverses target and explanatory roles. These are conditions on the supplied transition relations; they do not choose a branch without a premise.
550	
551	If \(R\) relates \(D\) to \(E\) and \(S\) relates \(E\) to \(F\), their composite is
552	
553	\[
554	(S\circ R)(z,w)
555	\iff\exists y\,[zRy\land ySw].
556	\]
557	
558	Forward preservation composes: use the \(R\)-witness for the first match and the \(S\)-witness for the second. The backward condition composes by the same argument. Query preservation composes when the intermediate query and scope are the same. Mere overlap of two unrelated interpretations is insufficient.
559	
560	Equation (E) permits either the functional case or this relational case. The choice must be stated; the stronger claims of equivalence are not inferred from a one-sided simulation.
561	
562	## Approximate transport
563	
564	Suppose three representations have maps \(f:X\to Y\), \(g:Y\to Z\), and an actual map \(h:X\to Z\). If
565	
566	\[
567	d_Z(h(x),g(f(x)))\le\varepsilon
568	\]
569	
570	on a stated scope, then that bound is the claim. It does not automatically survive repeated use.
571	
572	For stepwise dynamics, suppose the discrepancy after one mapped step is at most \(\varepsilon\), and the represented next-step map is \(L\)-Lipschitz. Writing \(e_n\) for the discrepancy after \(n\) steps gives
573	
574	\[
575	e_{n+1}\le L e_n+\varepsilon.
576	\]
577	
578	With \(e_0=0\),
579	
580	\[
581	e_n\le\varepsilon\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}L^k.
582	\tag{T2}
583	\]
584	
585	**Proof.** Substitute the preceding bound into the recurrence and induct. ∎
586	
587	Without a Lipschitz bound, a stated modulus of continuity can replace multiplication by \(L\). Without either, a general accumulated-error bound does not follow. Approximation is not exact equivalence, and an exact question may not be silently replaced by an approximate one.
588	
589	## Historical truth and changed applicability
590	
591	A proposition indexed to \((p,\Sigma,h,e)\) remains that proposition when a later theory changes the current scope. A new index creates a new claim; it does not retroactively invalidate every true proposition at the old index.
592	
593	A later model may show that the earlier application was always mistaken. That changes the appraisal of an old claim, not the old world's truth. Alternatively, a later model may preserve an accurate approximation while explaining its limits. These are different cases. A transport must say which it is.
594	
595	# Criticism, evidence, and operative decisions
596	
597	## Histories, attention, and situations
598	
599	A history \(h\) is a set of occurrences with an acyclic causal precedence relation \(\prec_h\), together with its physical process interpretation. Semantic support and opposition need not be acyclic. Two existing arguments can oppose each other without either having caused an earlier event.
600	
601	For token-level claims, the physical interpretation of a history supplies process occurrences with their input and output ports, the port-to-port connections actually instantiated, and the component relations applied there. An **active route** is a connected subnetwork of those actual occurrences joining the named represented input to the named operative result. Its designation must satisfy the corresponding component relations and role bindings; it is not inferred from the presence of a similar sentence in a record. For reason-use and contribution claims the subnetwork must also have a nonconstant dependence on the relevant represented distinction under its declared contrasts. A dead branch, a cancelled signal with no downstream role, or a carrier detail that changes while the represented reason does not change cannot supply that dependence. Contingent alternatives and collective blocks remain available, so this condition does not equate contribution with single-variable necessity at the full endpoint.
602	
603	A situation \(\xi\) comprises the contents currently represented or available, active questions, current uses, appraisal acts, attention engagements, purposes, and the relevant links to the history. These are role relations, not compulsory explicit databases.
604	
605	An episode is a causally connected course of attention to an interpreted difficulty. It can contain overlapping subepisodes, change formulation, pause, resume, or become part of another episode. Attention is itself an activity in the history. Its organization and the values affecting it are potential criticism targets. The class imposes no maximizing attention function and no rule that the most recent objection receives priority.
606	
607	## A criticism and its bearing
608	
609	A criticism has a represented target \(z\), an alleged defect \(\delta\), grounds \(g\), and a proposed connection from \(g\) to \(\delta\) relative to a question. A defect is a specified failure condition on the target or its application: inconsistency, a false dependency, a missing distinction, an unsupported reference, a failed task, a misapplied rule, or another condition whose interpretation is supplied.
610	
611	Write \(p_\delta\) for the question about that alleged defect. Define
612	
613	\[
614	\operatorname{Bearing}(c,z,p)
615	\iff
616	\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E_c,p_\delta),
617	\tag{K1}
618	\]
619	
620	where \(\mathcal E_c\) is the criticism's interpreted structural account. The alleged defect must concern the stated target and respect. A counterexample to a universal claim is a simple structural case: the target's requirement and the counterexample cannot jointly hold.
621	
622	A criticism occurrence can exist when (K1) is false. Its grounds may be mistaken, its target misidentified, its inference invalid, or its relevance wrong. A mere adverse signal is not made into a criticism by giving it a negative label. It can become grounds for a criticism when an organization represents how it bears on a target.
623	
624	## Reason use is causal organization, not an output comparison
625	
626	A response uses a reason when the represented content of the objection participates in the organization's deliberative transition. The response state includes interpretations, provisional uses, methods, and continuing questions, not just a terminal action label.
627	
628	Formally, the realization supplies a response suborganization \(D_s\) with represented target, grounds, defect connection, and response-role ports. A reason-use witness is a structural map from the represented objection organization into that suborganization such that content-preserving recodings preserve the interpreted transition, relevant changes to the grounds or alleged defect have the changes specified by the system's operative deliberative rule, and the mapped objection is on an active dependency route of this response occurrence. The map must preserve internal role bindings, not merely the endpoint string.
629	
630	The operative deliberative rule can be wrong. **Understanding and using an invalid objection does not make it valid.** The definition concerns whether the system used the content, not whether it responded ideally. Its contrast contract must include a content-changing case, a content-preserving recoding, and the distinction between a change in the objection and an irrelevant carrier disturbance wherever those distinctions are claimed. These are semantic comparisons, not a mandatory battery of physical tests.
631	
632	Two objections can lead to the same decision for different represented reasons. A valid criticism can lead to retention when its alleged force has been misunderstood. An invalid criticism can lead to a mistaken revision. A refusal with no evidenced or modeled content-sensitive route must not be assigned a fictional reason.
633	
634	An observer may lack the data needed to establish the witness. That makes the attribution unresolved; it does not prove either understanding or its absence.
635	
636	## Standing and actual use
637	
638	Standing is the system's enacted permission to use a content in a particular application and respect. It may be explicit or inexplicit. An appraisal can change it without having earned prior certification. Generation alone does not logically entail it, but generation and provisional adoption may occur together in one physical event. Separating their meanings does not require separate timestamps or separate machines.
639	
640	A source's appearance in a prompt is a delivery fact. A named field asking for a criticism is an invitation fact. Actual use of the source as a premise, actual understanding, and actual criticism are semantic attributions. They are not automatically machine-maintainable facts merely because a host can maintain corresponding labels.
641	
642	For an argument application \(u\), let \(\operatorname{Prem}(u)\) be its declared essential premises, including interpretation and scope premises. Let \(\operatorname{Live}_j(d;u)\) indicate standing in appraisal \(j\), and let \(\operatorname{Lic}_j(u)\) and \(\operatorname{Scope}_j(u)\) indicate the enacted license and scope judgment. Define
643	
644	\[
645	\operatorname{Usable}_j(u)
646	\iff
647	\operatorname{Lic}_j(u)\land\operatorname{Scope}_j(u)
648	\land\forall d\in\operatorname{Prem}(u),
649	\operatorname{Live}_j(d;u).
650	\tag{K2}
651	\]
652	
653	The actor can violate this coherence condition. The model then represents an error in its appraisal. A record declaring a dependency does not establish that the dependency is actually essential; an error in that declaration is another criticism target.
654	
655	## Elimination without a truth machine
656	
657	Suppose a system withdraws an essential premise of \(u\). Equation (K2) no longer licenses \(u\). Another argument \(v\) for the same conclusion can remain usable. The conclusion is not thereby false. Withdrawing a criticism likewise does not establish the truth of its target.
658	
659	The thinker can remove a rejected conjecture from its current working use while retaining its occurrence for comparison or later criticism. It need not retain every rejected occurrence forever, and the absence of an archival copy does not undo a past creative event. Availability as a current target requires some representation of that target, not an append-only history of every earlier thought.
660	
661	A machine check can establish a limited proposition such as equality with source bytes or validity of a derivation relative to formal premises. Its interpretation can have real consequences. A passing execution cannot make the program's specification, the model of the experiment, or the claimed relevance immune to prose criticism.
662	
663	For a test whose reasoning is
664	
665	\[
666	T\land B\land I\ \Longrightarrow\ O,
667	\]
668	
669	an established \(\neg O\) yields
670	
671	\[
672	\neg(T\land B\land I).
673	\tag{K3}
674	\]
675	
676	It does not yield \(\neg T\) without additional premises about \(B\) and \(I\). Here \(B\) can include auxiliaries and \(I\) the observation interpretation. This is not an argument against testing. It states exactly what the test contradicts and where further criticism can matter.
677	
678	## Evidence receipts without false certainty
679	
680	Let an evidence leaf be a reference to an actual event and a particular interpreted claim about it. Its identity includes the event, the inspected relation, the interpretation, and the scope. Equal text in two events does not identify their provenance or metadata.
681	
682	A receipt is a derivation tree whose leaves are these references and whose internal nodes specify the inference actually used. Distinct sufficient routes remain distinct receipts. Conjunction combines the premises needed by that route; disjunction permits a witness from either side. A refutation by an independent disjunct must not inherit the disputed assumptions of an unused disjunct.
683	
684	For a claim \(\phi\), let \(P_j(\phi)\) be the set of currently usable receipts supporting it and \(N_j(\phi)\) those supporting its negation. The record can indicate that neither set, one set, or both sets are nonempty. These are descriptions of available arguments, not four kinds of reality.
685	
686	Negating a claim exchanges its positive and negative receipt sets. It does not turn an absent receipt into a negative observation. Thus missing evidence remains missing under negation. An explicitly named missing predecessor remains that missing predecessor; a different baseline may not be substituted without changing the claim.
687	
688	Eligibility is a separate predicate. An observation of a completed answer can be eligible for a content claim. A timeout may instead be evidence about delivery. The inability to evaluate a proposition is not a falsifying observation of the proposition.
689	
690	This receipt construction is optional descriptive mathematics. Ordinary prose need not arrive with a tree, source fields, or a machine-verifiable witness to enter inquiry. The point is that an interpretation of its reasoning must not silently lose its actual dependencies.
691	
692	# Understanding, provenance, and creative events
693	
694	## Realized use rather than logical omniscience
695	
696	For a content organization \(c\), a use task specifies requests to employ its represented relations in a declared family of problem contexts and the corresponding internal or external semantic outcomes. The requests can include interpreting a component, following a dependence, relating an implication to a question, or treating the content as a target of criticism. The outcomes are changes in represented organization, not necessarily sentences.
697	
698	A system **understands \(c\) in a stated respect** when a represented realization of \(c\) is integrated into its own problem-directed activity and supports the corresponding content-governed uses. The realization must preserve relevant role bindings and at least the discriminations in the declared use contract. It must permit \(c\) to be treated as a conjectural target rather than merely enact a received instruction. The retained-capability definition in the constructor section gives the modal meaning of “supports.”
699	
700	A system may understand a false theory. The use task can concern the theory's own organization while its application to the world fails. Understanding is not defined as agreement, correct prediction of the world, or actual success of the explanation.
701	
702	Let
703	
704	\[
705	\operatorname{Deploy}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,\xi;U)
706	\]
707	
708	hold when the attributed system possesses such a realization and an owned capability for the declared use task \(U\) at \(\xi\). The repertoire \(R_{\beta,\ell}(s,\xi)\) consists of the contents deployable in at least one nontrivial explanatory use respect. Storage, universal mathematical consequence, and possible acquisition after further learning are not sufficient for membership.
709	
710	This is a deliberately structural understanding proposal. A generic simulator is not automatically an understander because it produces the right trajectories. Its represented reference, integration into problem-directed activity, and ability to make the simulated account a critical target must also be present. Conversely, no substrate or notation is excluded merely because it is a simulation or a program.
711	
712	## Construction and transfer
713	
714	A construction witness concerns an actual suborganization of a history. It identifies the controlled processes, incoming carriers and already operative organizations, the bindings constructed or reconstructed, and the resulting representation. Its physical and semantic maps must preserve the relevant component structure, as in (E).
715	
716	An elementary **transfer** is content-preserving carriage of an already integrated organization at the stated grain. An elementary **binding construction** changes or establishes a relation between represented parts in the recipient's operative organization. These are classifications of actual transformations under the interpretation, not intrinsic types conferred by a model's invitation or by a host event label.
717	
718	Define \(\operatorname{Build}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,h,e)\) when an actual subhistory owned or controlled by \(s\), delimited at \(e\), prepares a represented organization for an attempted explanatory use of \(c\), contains a nontrivial binding construction relevant to that use, and is not merely a composition of content-preserving transfers of the already operative organization. A structural account of that subhistory must connect the constructed binding to the resulting use. Electricity supply, incidental causal ancestry, and ownership of an output file do not by themselves meet the condition.
719	
720	“Owned or controlled” refers to the boundary's actual action-producing organization. In a collaboration it can be distributed. A list of contributors is not a construction witness. Overlapping attributions are possible when their respective causal-organizational claims are true; they do not create a numerical credit allocation.
721	
722	A learner may receive a complete exposition and nevertheless construct the bindings through which it becomes usable to that learner. That is reconstructive construction, not historical firstness. A relay may deliver the same exposition without such construction. A physically faithful copy of an already functioning cognitive organization, if permitted by the relevant physics, must not be pronounced a fresh invention merely because the recipient's address is new. The interpretation must distinguish transfer of an operative organization from its reconstruction.
723	
724	The construction predicate is not an assertion that every acquisition must be creative. It is an explicit provenance condition to be established. All claims about functional copying remain subject to physical realization, including restrictions on what information attributes can be copied.
725	
726	## Newness, acquisition, and reacquisition
727	
728	Fix a system boundary, grain, history, and continuity criterion before assessing an event. Let
729	
730	\[
731	R_{<e}(s,h)
732	=
733	\bigcup_{\xi\text{ before }e}R_{\beta,\ell}(s,\xi),
734	\]
735	
736	including the initial repertoire within the stipulated continuity. Define
737	
738	\[
739	\operatorname{New}(s,c,h,e)
740	\iff
741	\neg\exists d\in R_{<e}(s,h),
742	\ d\equiv_\ell c.
743	\tag{N}
744	\]
745	
746	The equivalence is structural at the stated grain, not string equality or similarity. Forgotten prior understanding belongs to \(R_{<e}\) when the claim is first creation by that continuing organization. Reacquisition can therefore be an achievement without being first creation.
747	
748	Acquisition concerns absence from the immediately prior deployable repertoire and presence afterward. Newness concerns the whole stipulated historical baseline. Construction concerns provenance. These relations can come apart.
749	
750	An incomplete archive leaves a historical claim uncertain. It does not make the absent content historically new. Initializing a new system boundary with an already functioning organization must include that organization in its baseline rather than manufacture novelty by forgetting its initialization.
751	
752	## An originative explanatory act
753	
754	An attempted account is a represented organization actually used to address a recognized difficulty, whether or not it satisfies (E). Write this relation as \(\operatorname{Attempt}(s,c,p,h,e)\). Its interpretation includes the active question and the content's operative role; a task label alone is insufficient.
755	
756	Define
757	
758	\[
759	\operatorname{Origin}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,p,h,e)
760	\iff
761	\operatorname{Attempt}(s,c,p,h,e)
762	\land\operatorname{New}(s,c,h,e)
763	\land\operatorname{Build}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,h,e).
764	\tag{G}
765	\]
766
